passages.text: An autopilot for a boat, running on the Infineon KIT_A2G_TC375_LITE board (AURIX TC375, three CPU cores). There are two variants: * SMALL BOAT (default): outboard engine. The software controls the steering motor (no angle sensor: the angle is estimated), the throttle servo and the gear servo (Forward / Neutral / Reverse). It uses compass, gyro and GPS. Driving modes: MANUAL (joystick), HEADING LOCK and AUTO (waypoint program). It navigates without GPS (dead reckoning), calibrates itself (TRAINING), limits the engine power until you raise it on purpose, and logs everything to an SD card.

* BIG BOAT: rudder with an angle sensor, heading hold only. The board has not arrived yet. All of the logic is written and tested in a PC simulation with a simulated boat. The drivers for the Stage 1 parts (IMU, GPS, steering motor driver, buttons, end stops, emergency stop, buzzer, microSD, USB link) are written but not yet tried on the real board; a few parts are still empty "stubs" (see chapter 17). FIRST_TEST.md is the checklist for the first power-up and the first steering test.
core 0 the control loop (20 Hz): modes, steering, engine, PC link
CPU1 an independent safety monitor (checks core 0 every 1 ms)
core 2 the logger (writes the SD card)

A PC ground station shows the boat live and sends commands, over the board's USB cable or to the simulator. Two kinds of joystick can drive the boat (chosen in the ground station): the hard-wired analog joystick, or a USB Thrustmaster T.16000M stick + TWCS throttle, read by a small Teensy 4.1 "bridge" board (chapter 8).
app/ The autopilot itself. Pure C, no hardware code. The same files run on the board and in the PC simulation.

smallboat.c small-boat controller: modes, engine, steering, faults modes.c mode manager: the ONLY place that changes the mode autopilot.c steering core (heading hold, outboard angle estimate) program.c AUTO waypoint programs (check, store with checksum) powerlim.c power limit (30 % / 5 % at start, raise / drop) servo.c the ONLY code that writes the throttle servo monitor.c the independent safety monitor (runs on CPU1) joystick.c the joystick, whatever its source (analog or USB) joybridge.c USB joystick: frames from the bridge, fault checks joymap.c joystick source + USB button map (saved with checksum) jsframe.c the bridge frame format (also compiled into the bridge) gear.c, throttle.c, nav.c, dr.c, training.c, calib.c proto.c, link.c PC link (frames, telemetry, commands) timing.c CPU time per cycle, overruns logq.c, logrec.c, logcore0.c, logfields.h, logger.c logging
hal/hal.h The list of hardware functions the app may use. hal/hal_tc375.c The real board versions of those functions.
hal/hal_pins.h Every pin of the board in one table (= WIRING.md).
hal/tc_*.c The board drivers (UART, SPI, IMU, GPS, ADC, SD card).
Cpu0_Main.c core 0: start-up, watchdog, the 20 Hz loop. "#define BOAT_VARIANT_BIG" at the top selects the big boat.
Cpu1_Main.c CPU1: the safety monitor loop (1 kHz).
Cpu2_Main.c core 2: the logger loop.
sim/ PC simulation, all tests, simulated boat for the ground station. NOT part of the board build.
boats/ One file per boat (name + Tailscale address + equipment: generator cap, relays, thrusters; no secrets): the ground station's boat list (chapter 5). Comes with every clone.
groundstation/ PC ground station and log tools (Python).
gateway/ gateway PC software (Python; Ubuntu 24.04 / Windows 11): remote access, log copy, cameras, sync. Setup step by step: gateway/README.md.
bridge/ Teensy 4.1 firmware for the USB joystick (PlatformIO). Setup step by step: bridge/README.md.
tools/ mapreport.py: memory report from the ADS build.
WIRING.md Wiring: joysticks (analog and USB bridge), panel buttons, servos, SD card, USB.
CLAUDE.md The project rules (also read by Claude).
MANUAL.txt This file. Libraries/, Configurations/ Generated by AURIX Development Studio. NEVER edit them.

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 1. HDG LOCK with the throttle ON BOARD: HDG LOCK (panel). Move the "lever" slider up a little (above 55 %) -> the boat moves; -1 / +1 change the heading. Lever back to 50, STBY or STANDBY -> stop.

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 2. A SAVE DRIVER screen: the big SAVE button (or a SAVE button on a joystick). Screen 2, Cameras tab: "SAVING until ..." and the event in demo_run\ssd\video\events\. 3. A channel switch Screen 2, Network tab: channel RF -> MANUAL -> within 60 s KEEP. The top line of the driver screen shows the channel. STARLINK is the emergency channel: data saver, no sync, a yellow banner.

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 4. An AUTO mission Screen 2, Program tab: Load file -> demo\demo_mission.json (6 waypoints, 6-12 kn) -> Check depth -> Upload to boat. Then Take HELM and press the mode button AUTO: the DRIVER screen asks -> ACCEPT; then ON BOARD: CONFIRM within 10 s. The boat drives the program (map tab). To go faster than 30 %: Raise fwd, type the code, Send code, ON BOARD CONFIRM - one step at a time.

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 5a. A kayak WITHOUT AIS (only the camera can see it) Double-click DEMO_KAYAK.bat while driving (HDG LOCK or AUTO): an obstacle 120 m ahead for 40 s. Driver screen / maps: the orange sector, OBSTACLE AHEAD + SAVE (STAGE 2). With STAGE 3 switched on (Cameras tab, driver ACCEPT) AUTO slows down. The front camera of the demo shows a sea video with the AI colours (when the model is installed: tools\get_vision_python.py, get_vision_model.py, get_vision_samples.py; else only these injected detections).

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 5. An AIS collision situation While AUTO runs (or in HDG LOCK): double-click DEMO_SHIP.bat. A ferry comes from starboard. Screen 2, AIS tab: the ship turns yellow, then red (CPA / TCPA). AUTO slows down, then passes astern of the ferry (route on the map) and goes back to the leg; the driver screen shows the ship line; COLLISION RISK starts a SAVE. In HDG LOCK the driver screen PROPOSES a heading: ACCEPT / REJECT.

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 6. Remote driving with a USB joystick Plug the joystick into this PC. Tools, Remote tab: Find joysticks, choose it, Take HELM, then REMOTE MANUAL on screen 1; ON BOARD: CONFIRM within 10 s (an UNCREWED boat - no CONFIRM: it starts at once, only with the shore stick centred and the lever at neutral). Mode REMOTE MANUAL: the shore joystick drives (max 20 % / 5 %). Any move of the ON BOARD stick or lever, or STANDBY, takes control back at once. There is no RELEASE: to end it, choose another mode (STANDBY, AUTO, DP).

passages.heading: WHAT TO TRY
passages.text: 7. The joystick always wins During AUTO move the ON BOARD stick X slider or press TAKE: MANUAL at once, and an automatic SAVE. Resume the program: AUTO resume (captain) + ON BOARD CONFIRM. The REAR and FRONT-2 demo cameras show test pictures (grey, a moving bar, a time code); FRONT-1 shows a sea video (MaSTr1325 pictures, CC BY 4.0) when tools\get_vision_samples.py was run.

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: * The station refuses to connect if the gateway is another boat (each gateway knows its own name - gateway config "boat"). * Connect -> the name check is AUTOMATIC (the gateway's welcome must name this boat) -> "✓ name verified" and this station takes HELM AT ONCE if HELM is free (a captain / a station without a crew role; a copilot never takes it; held by another station = a message, take it in the HELM panel if you must). THE BOAT FILE (format 2): "format": 2, id, name, tailscale_ip, gateway_port, and the boat's equipment:

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: generator_max_pct the generator's throttle cap in neutral (chapter 7), 0 or missing = generator disabled; the AURIX caps it at 30 % whatever the file says.

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: relays the relay board's channels (step 6): n (channel), name_el / name_en, type onoff | momentary (a board-timed pulse, max_s <= 5 s) | latching | timed (off after max_s), group engine (IGNITION, STARTER, SHUTOFF: the engine rules) | trim | extra, pair (the other relay of an interlocked pair - must point back, never both on), show_hud (also on screen 1), power_up off | on | keep (engine relays: only off - never switched by themselves), role (engine relays ONLY, required): starter (a momentary relay, max_s <= 5 s) | ignition | shutoff (onoff / latching), each once.

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: thrusters the DP thrusters (chapter 7, DP THRUSTERS): bow / stern: max_pct (0 = not fitted), run_s / rest_s (heat budget: the longest run, the rest after it), jog_m (one JOG step), spot_alarm_m (the off-spot alarm; both DP).

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: A file without "format" is the old v1: it still loads, with generator disabled, no relays and no thrusters. A file that fails the checks (wrong type, a pair that is not mutual, a momentary relay longer than 5 s, an engine relay with power_up on / keep, an engine relay without its role, an engine relay in a pair (SHUTOFF must never be blocked), a STARTER that is not momentary, a relay named STARTER / ΜΙΖΑ without the role "starter" ...) is listed as INVALID FILE with the reason and is never connected: fix the file.

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: When this station holds HELM (in STANDBY) it pushes the file's settings to the boat (generator cap, the relay table, the DP thruster settings): the cap and the thruster settings are RAM only - a boat restart gets them again; the relay table is kept in the boat's data flash and a DIFFERENT one needs the joystick CONFIRM (chapter 7, RELAY BOARD). While a relay still has to be switched off (a TIMED relay running, an OFF the board has not confirmed yet, a pulse, a queued SHUTOFF) no new table is taken: the boat answers "relay stop pending: the relay table changes after it" and the station sends the table again (and asks for the CONFIRM) only after it.

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: Screen 2's relays panel then says "the relay table waits: a relay stop / timer is still pending". There is NO time limit on this wait (a stop is never dropped): switch the timed relay OFF to end it early; an OFF the board must still confirm waits until a SILENT board answers again - a board that stays silent blocks the table change until it answers or the AURIX restarts. The event list shows "boat file RF49D: generator max 25 %" and "boat file RF49D: DP thrusters, bow 100 %, stern 100 %".

passages.heading: CHOOSING THE BOAT (the first line of the top-left STATUS panel)
passages.text: "Other address ..." (Tools - Connection): the connection box (COM5, tcp:..., gw:host:port) for the board on USB, the simulator, the demo and service; then there is no boat check.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: The boat is ALWAYS in the centre and the map moves under it; north is always up (no course-up); the boat symbol turns with the heading. Zoom: "Zoom +" / "Zoom −" (bottom middle), the mouse wheel or + / -. A drag pans the map for a moment (e.g. to edit a far waypoint): it goes back to the boat by itself 10 s after the last touch, or at once with "Back to boat" (or the key B). The panels are see-through and never cover the boat or the area around it.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: A click on a panel's title folds it to the title (▸) or opens it again (▾); DRAG a panel's title to put the panel anywhere (it never goes over the boat or over the bars); both remembered on this PC; RESET TO DEFAULT (bar 2 or the tools window) puts every panel back. STANDBY (big red, bottom-left corner) is ALWAYS there, also with every panel folded. THE LOOK (step 13n1, owner 2026-10-31): red = alarms (WARNING) only, amber = CAUTION; the only red buttons are STANDBY and SAVE (owner 2026-11-04); other information is black or white by its background; the CONNECTED lamp is white. Everything you can press or type into has a square frame.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Only 3 text sizes everywhere (very important / heading / information); "Aa" (bar 2, screen 1's bar, the tools window, the academy windows) = small / normal / large text, saved on this PC. MODE BAR (top middle, always there, can't be hidden): [STANDBY] [HDG LOCK] [AUTO] [REMOTE] [MANEUVER] [DP] [MANUAL] · [BATTLE SHORT] The current mode is inverted (white, black bold, a little bigger). A mode that is not allowed now is grey; a click on it says why ("no route", "captain only", "MANUAL only with the joystick on board" ...). A click on an allowed one changes the mode - the boat checks every request again with its own rules (HELM, licence, CONFIRM, the stick centred).

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: REMOTE / MANEUVER: the captain with the manual licence (or a licensed single operator); HDG LOCK from the PC only UNCREWED from REMOTE / MANEUVER (CREWED: the panel button on board); AUTO = AUTO START of the route on the boat; DP = SPOT; MANUAL is shown but never pressable from the PC. A copilot's mode change waits for the captain's ACCEPT (STANDBY never). BATTLE SHORT asks for the commander's authorisation code (the tooltip says so).

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: TWO BARS at the bottom (between STANDBY and the logo; ▾ at the left end hides a bar to a slim handle, ⇅ moves both bars to the top under the mode bar and back): Bar 1 heading −10 −1 [target] +1 +10 · AUTO Pause / Resume / Skip · ROUTE · MAX SPEED · GEOFENCE (each opens its small panel just above the bar while you use it; the button again closes it) · LINK TIME − + (captain with HELM) · RESTORE POWER when offered Bar 2 the nearest AIS ship + CPA · the last message · Zoom − / Zoom + (/ Back to boat) · BOAT (the boat dropdown) · TRACKS ·

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: NEW TRACK · the recording group [SCR · ●5' · ●1h] (see SCREEN RECORDING below) · CAMERA (through a gateway) · Tools · Aa · RESET TO DEFAULT

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: TRACK (step 13n3): the boat's track is the WHITE line on the map (BLACK on a light map; dim red at night), also on screen 1's mini map. Every point is kept (time, position, speed, heading) - no limit - and written at once to this PC's disk (groundstation/tracks/): after a crash or a restart the track is there again and goes on. ONE track PER BOAT: another boat shows its own track, never a mix. Click on the line = the time and the speed there (on the line + the message bar; a click elsewhere removes it). NEW TRACK: a YES / NO question, then the current track is saved as <date>_<time>_<boat> (e.g.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: 2026-10-31_0834_TRYGON-1, the time of its first point) and a new line starts. TRACKS: the list of the saved tracks (date, boat, duration, nm); select one or more (Ctrl / Shift + click) -> SHOW = on the map as a GREY DASHED line with its date, any day, any boat; HIDE; REMOVE FROM MAP (the file stays); EXPORT GPX (the selected ones) / CURRENT TRACK TO GPX / IMPORT GPX (GPX 1.1: Google Earth, OpenCPN, plotters; a file with a DTD, without track points, over 64 MB or with more than 200 000 points is refused). Two stations on one PC on the same boat: the first one writes the file, the other keeps its track in memory only.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: A full disk: the message "the track is not written to the disk" - the track goes on in memory. The track never changes anything on the boat. SCREEN RECORDING + KEEP (step 13n4) - on BOTH screens (screen 2 bar 2, screen 1's bottom bar [REC · SCR · SAVE · ●5' · ●1h]):

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: SCR records BOTH screens of THIS PC (screen 1 + screen 2, each its own window) at a lower resolution (at most 1280 wide, 5 pictures a second, H.264 - NVENC when the PC has an NVIDIA card, else x264) into 1-minute files; only the LAST 60 MINUTES are kept (a ring, about 0.3 GB per hour). The button shows ●SCR (white) while it records; press again to stop. It runs as its own low-priority program: it never slows the station and never affects driving. It starts again by itself at the next start if it was on.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Not enough free disk (under 2 GB): it does not start / stops by itself with a message - nothing already kept is lost. A screen that is closed (only one window) simply has no file. Needs ffmpeg on this PC (as the gateway). Folder: groundstation\screenrec\ (ring\SCREEN-1, ring\SCREEN-2, events\<id>\).

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: SAVE (the normal one) also keeps the screen part: the same event id and time, 10 min before + 2 min after, like the cameras.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: ●5' ●1h KEEP PERMANENTLY the last 5 / 60 minutes of BOTH screens of this PC AND the boat's 4 cameras at FULL resolution (one event id / time): the screen part in groundstation\screenrec\events\<id>\, the camera part on the boat's SSD (video\events\<id>\, not uploaded to the shore - it is big; copy it from the gateway PC when needed). Kept files leave the rings and are NEVER deleted automatically (delete the folders by hand). A SAVE that the gateway adds to an already open camera event: the screen part records the cameras' id ("camera_event" in its event.json). If the station closes abruptly, the screen recording (ffmpeg) stops with it.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: The message says what was kept: "SAVED – SCREENS + CAMERAS 5 MIN / 1 HOUR"; when a ring is shorter than asked, what exists is kept and the message says so ("CAMERAS: only 20 min available"); no gateway / a VIEWER / a full SSD = the screens are kept, the message says why the cameras are not. The gateway's camera ring is 60 min by default (Cameras tab).

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: CAMERA VIEW (step 13n2, for the copilot's PC above all): CAMERA on bar 2 shows one of the boat's cameras over the whole of screen 2. Bar 1 then holds FRONT-1 / FRONT-2 / REAR-L / REAR-R and MAP; MAP or Esc = back to the map. Green on the picture: the camera, the mode, heading, speed, throttle + gear. The mode bar, STANDBY and the alarm panel stay; the other panels give way; the map can't be edited under it. The camera is sent to this PC ONLY while the view is open.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: A copilot gets the LIGHTER stream (the camera's low stream, 10 pictures a second), and the captain's video has priority: when the video to the stations is more than the gateway allows (cameras.copilot_budget_kbps, 6000 kbit/s), the copilot's view is cut FIRST ("VIDEO REDUCED FOR THE CAPTAIN"), back by itself when it fits again (10 s). DATA SAVER / STARLINK: no camera view at all. A view never changes anything on the boat. "AI" (a small framed white badge) is shown ONLY where a neural network works: the obstacle detection (eWaSR) and the Piper voice. AI only warns and may slow down - it never steers. Collision avoidance, the autopilot and the shallow-water checks are NOT AI.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Top left STATUS: first line = the boat dropdown + the lamp CONNECTED + "✓ name verified" (see CHOOSING THE BOAT); the mode, the POWER LIMIT with Raise fwd / Raise rev / Lower; heading, target, rate of turn, gear, throttle ("asked" when more was asked than allowed), outboard, GPS (fix, source, uncertainty), speed / course over ground

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Top right ALARMS (always shown, also with every panel folded; no alarm = a one-line header): every active alarm, one per line, the most severe first; red = WARNING, amber = CAUTION, blue = advisory. An alarm not yet acknowledged ON THIS PC flashes (the same clock as the GENERAL lamps on screen 1; the text stays, only the fill blinks); acknowledged ones and advisories are steady. "+N more" when more are active than fit. ACK ALARM = first silences THIS PC (lamps + repeating sound, like the GENERAL lamp of screen 1), then the boat's acknowledge (clears only alarms whose cause is gone; from any station).

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Space / A on screen 2 = silence this PC only (also with screen 1 closed; not while you type in a field). Disconnected (or "not this boat"): the old data is dropped - no alarms, no sound, "Not connected"; after a new connection only that boat's alarms. Under it: HELM / ROLES: who holds HELM, your role (CAPTAIN / COPILOT, licence), the captain's name; Take HELM, Release (UNCREWED: releasing = a lost link, you are asked first), Role swap, Screen 1, Single operator.

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: LINK: data OK / NO DATA; every internet channel (4G, 4G2, RF, STARLINK) with quality bars, latency, loss, up / down (▶ = the one in use); the profile CREWED / UNCREWED; NEAR SHORE xx m / open sea xx m from shallow water / shore distance unknown (counts as near); while the link is lost: the seconds to the engine kill (or "near the shore: engine kill at idle"); ENGINE KILLED - RESTART (Engine page) or reset on board

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Bottom left CONTROL (a slim strip above the bars): the AUTO state, AUTO RETURN, generator, the DP rows; the captain's answers to your actions (copilot: WAITING / ACCEPTED / REJECTED). With the simulator also: panel HDG LOCK / STANDBY and the joystick CONFIRM. (The modes are on the MODE BAR, the heading / AUTO pause / ROUTE / MAX SPEED / GEOFENCE / LINK TIME on bar 1.)

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Bottom right TRAFFIC: the collision-avoidance state and a proposal, the nearest AIS ships (name, distance, bearing, CPA, TCPA; red = danger, amber = warning; a click opens the details), "AIS doesn't show small craft"; under it the logo

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Top middle under the mode bar: banners, only when needed (the alarms are in the ALARMS panel): LINK LOST / ENGINE KILLED, PRESS JOYSTICK CONFIRM, REMOTE / MANEUVER / JOYSTICK IN CONTROL, pickup, FIRST TEST, UNCREWED, shallow water ahead, collision risk, STARLINK EMERGENCY, single operator, boat not confirmed, the editing help

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Above bars the chart note "Not for navigation ..."

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: Menu bar Windows (screen 1, F11, move to a monitor, swap F12), Tools (every page), View (dark / light theme for BOTH screens, the map layers + range rings), Language

passages.heading: SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS
passages.text: TOOLS window (button "Tools" or the Tools menu; a list of pages on the left): Connection, Control (sea state, training, the simulator's panel + USB joystick), Program (the route as a table, save / load a file), AIS (details), Plot, Config, Joystick (+ the stick / lever picture), Cameras, Remote (the shore joystick: device, axes, "send joystick"), Network, System, Bench, Engine (IGNITION / START / SHUTOFF, RESTART - chapter 7, ENGINE CONTROLS), Sound, Events Where this manual says "... tab" (Program tab, Joystick tab, Cameras tab ...), it means that page of the TOOLS window.

passages.heading: EDITING ON THE MAP (the copilot's work; the captain can do it too)
passages.text: ROUTE "Edit route": a click on the map adds a waypoint at the end, a drag moves one, a right click deletes one; − / + set the speed of the new waypoints (while editing: of all of them). "Send route" = upload to the boat (refused across shallow water or out of the geofence: the leg and the position are shown). Until then the panel says NOT SENT (the route is amber on the map).

passages.heading: EDITING ON THE MAP (the copilot's work; the captain can do it too)
passages.text: MAX SPEED − / + then "Set": the highest leg speed the boat accepts (parameter max_leg_kn).

passages.heading: EDITING ON THE MAP (the copilot's work; the captain can do it too)
passages.text: GEOFENCE "Edit fence": clicks add corners (3 .. 50), a drag moves one, a right click deletes one; "Send fence" -> the GATEWAY keeps it and refuses every route upload / AUTO start that leaves it (code 120); "Clear fence" removes it. It never steers and never changes the throttle. Shown on the map: green = in force, amber dashed = being edited / not sent.

passages.heading: EDITING ON THE MAP (the copilot's work; the captain can do it too)
passages.text: A copilot's route, max speed and geofence (like every driving command) wait for the captain's ACCEPT on screen 1 (10 s, else refused): the Control panel shows WAITING, then ACCEPTED or REJECTED. The captain's own go straight through; single operator = the own confirmation.

passages.heading: EDITING ON THE MAP (the copilot's work; the captain can do it too)
passages.text: Every command gets an answer: OK, or why not (e.g. "JOYSTICK IS IN CONTROL", "only in STANDBY", "program refused: leg speed out of range (waypoint 3)"). Losing the PC for 3 s gives the alarm "PC LINK LOST" (and drops the power limit) but never stops or starts anything.
Every text on the screens (screen 1, screen 2 + its tools window, alarms, buttons, questions, bench test) comes from two plain text files:

SWITCH: the Language menu of screen 2, or on the driver screen the ΕΛ / EN button (key L). It changes at once on every window - no restart - and is remembered on this PC (groundstation\gs_settings.json, not in git). The VOICE language is chosen separately (Sound tab), e.g. Greek screens with English voice.

EDIT THE WORDS YOURSELF: open the file in VS Code (it is UTF-8 text): key = text * never change the key (left of "="); change the text freely * keep every {name} of a line (the program puts a number / name there); you may move it inside the text

* \n starts a new line; lines starting with # are comments * restart the ground station (or switch the language twice) * run python groundstation\test_lang.py : it checks that both files have the same keys and the same {names} (tools\check.sh runs it too)

The "say." lines are what the VOICE says (chapter 5D): write numbers as words and whole phrases (the Greek voice garbles a single short word). The "gw." lines translate sentences that come from the gateway in English (proposals, refusals): their ENGLISH text must stay exactly as the gateway writes it. WHAT STAYS IN ENGLISH (on purpose): the logs, the gateway's audit, the protocol, recordings and test reports use English + event codes, so an analysis works the same whatever language the screens had.

"Driver screen" (top bar) or Windows menu. The FRONT camera fills the whole window; everything else is drawn ON the video with a dark see-through backing and black-outlined text, readable over bright sea, sky and sun. One colour: all information on the video is GREEN (no white); RED = alarms only, AMBER = caution only; night mode = dim red.
+----------+ MODE (+ target heading) [GENERAL WARNING] +----------+
| REAR-L | channel latency POWER [GENERAL CAUTION] | REAR-R |
bar FRONT camera + AR overlays (5B AR) (one per line)
GEAR SPEED depth waypoint AIS outboard angle mini map ROT G
heading tape ... REC vision clock mission [SAVE]
Top left/right rear cameras as MIRRORS (picture flipped), small label; "VIDEO FROZEN" / "NO VIDEO" over a dead one

Top centre MODE big (+ target heading in HDG LOCK / AUTO); internet channel + latency (green < 250 ms, yellow, red > 600 ms; STARLINK EMERGENCY in a red box); POWER limit (amber when raised); "data x s old" when the telemetry is late

GENERAL WARNING (red) / GENERAL CAUTION (amber): lit by a new alarm of that level. One click (or Space / A) acknowledges BOTH and silences the repeating sound ON THIS PC. It sends nothing to the boat (the boat's ALARM ACK stays the captain's button). A newer alarm lights it again.

ALARMS the ONE place for alarms on this screen: the right column, directly under the right mirror. One alarm per line, the most severe first; red = WARNING, amber = CAUTION. An alarm not yet acknowledged ON THIS PC FLASHES (the same clock as the GENERAL lamps; the text stays, only the fill blinks); acknowledged ones and advisories are steady. "+N more" when more are active than fit. Shown at every declutter level, never over the middle of the picture.
Notices directly under the alarms, same style: press CONFIRM, pickup, single operator, collision line, shallow water ahead, front camera lost, FIRST TEST
Left throttle bar (0..100 %), amber line = power limit, amber band = cut by slamming, speed-trend arrow, GEAR as a big F / N / R (R amber)

Right SPEED very big + speed tape (+ AUTO set speed, trend); DEPTH from the chart at the boat (red below the shallow limit, amber below twice it; "no chart" if none); next WAYPOINT n/N, distance + bearing, ETA (clock), time to go; nearest AIS THREAT (name, CPA, TCPA, distance; red = danger); RATE OF TURN dial (+-15 deg/s); G-METER for slamming (bar = last impact, yellow + red lines = limits, marker = peak of the last 10 s)
Lower centre OUTBOARD angle (+-40 deg) and the CDI: how far off the planned track (AUTO; scale = 2 x the arrival radius, at least +-50 m)
Bottom right MINI MAP (dark, never white): depth chart, sea marks, AIS, own track, the program, active waypoint, DR circle
Above the bar the HEADING TAPE with the target mark (its own box)

Bottom bar (step 13n1) ONE thin bar across the whole width, in groups with small gaps: [ΕΛ/EN · NIGHT · DECLUTTER · FILL / FIT · Aa] [AR · OBSTACLES with the white "AI" badge + the vision status] [LAYOUT (+ CLEAR SLOWDOWN / RESTORE POWER when offered)] [REC (red dot) or NOT RECORDING · SCR (●SCR white while this PC records its screens) · SAVE (framed, big enough to hit) · ●5' · ●1h (step 13n4, see screen 2's SCREEN RECORDING)] [battery, generator, clock + mission time (since the first mode other than STANDBY)]. The bar is never hidden (every declutter level); SAVE and the GENERAL WARNING / CAUTION lamps never go away.
Colours on the video: every information GREEN; red only for a WARNING, amber for a CAUTION; NIGHT = dim red.
KEYS on the driver screen: Space / A acknowledge N night D declutter
V fill / fit L language E edit layout G all AR on / off O obstacle
overlay F11 full screen F12 swap with screen 2
Ctrl+Shift+1..9 this window to monitor 1..9

FILL / FIT: fill = the picture covers the window, cropped evenly; fit = the whole picture with black bars. NIGHT: dim red, darker picture, quieter sounds (5D). Remembered. DECLUTTER: FULL (all) -> NORMAL (no rate of turn, G-meter, CDI) -> MINIMAL (speed, heading, mode, gear, alarms only - also no AR). Remembered.

EDIT LAYOUT (LAYOUT button or E): every box gets a square frame. Drag a box by its middle to move it, drag the small square at its bottom-right corner to resize it (also the two mirrors: make a mirror bigger or smaller this way), the x / + in its top corner hides / shows it. RESET TO DEFAULT, DONE. Saved in groundstation\hud_layout.json (per PC). Outside the edit mode nothing can be moved by accident.

QUESTIONS (step 13p, owner 2026-10-31): a copilot's action for the captain's ACCEPT, a collision-avoidance proposal, the slamming power restore, an obstacle note - appear in the LOWER part of screen 1, just above the bottom bar (never over the centre of the picture), always the same VERTICAL layout: the question, [YES] on top, [NO] underneath (full width, framed; the selected one is filled = inverted), the countdown below; no answer = rejected.

The single operator's own confirmation (a window on screen 2) has the same layout, and so have the station's settings questions (strict channel, emergency, monitor trip test, HELM release UNCREWED, single operator on, crew swap; owner 2026-11-04): there NO is pre-selected; keys: Up / Down choose (the framed, filled one is the choice), Enter or Space answer with the choice shown, Esc or closing the window = NO. Answer with the mouse, or on the shore joystick (T.16000M stick + TWCS lever):

TRIGGER (stick button 1) = answer with the selected choice. YES is pre-selected, so the trigger alone = a fast ACCEPT. It counts only when the question has been shown for at least 0.5 s and only as a NEW press (a trigger held from before must be let go and pressed again).
thumb button (button 2) = a quick NO (REJECT), same 0.5 s rule.

stick forward / back = select YES / NO (more than 40 %, a fresh move from the centre) - only in STANDBY, AUTO, HDG LOCK and DP. In MANEUVER the stick forward / back is the gear, in REMOTE MANUAL it does nothing (the gear is on the lever).
hat up / down = select YES / NO in every mode.

A station that drives with the stick's Y as the throttle (no lever: "lever" off in the Remote tab): the stick forward / back never selects there - use the hat (the Remote tab says which). ONE PRESS NEVER DOES TWO THINGS: while a question is open the trigger answers it and is NOT sent to the boat (also not the press that answered, until you let it go; the gateway keeps it back too). With no question open the trigger works as before (UNCREWED HDG LOCK steered by hand: the new locked heading, chapter 7). The CONFIRM button on the TWCS (the boat's CONFIRM for AUTO start, power raise ... in UNCREWED) is unchanged. There is NO release button.

Moving the stick forward / back to select an answer moves nothing on the boat (tested: sim SY1). Default buttons (groundstation\shore_joystick.json): trigger 1, thumb ("reject_button") 2, SAVE ("save_button") 4, CONFIRM = TWCS button 4, hat = the stick's hat ("hat"; Linux: its axis number). An older file keeps its own SAVE button. A button mapped twice is not used for answers.

MANUAL DRIVING STARTS HERE (the captain with the manual licence; also a single operator with the licence): REMOTE MANUAL and MANEUVER (the buttons above the bottom-left row). UNCREWED boat: ONE press - it starts at once, only with the shore stick centred and the TWCS lever at neutral at that moment (otherwise "centre the joystick", nothing starts). CREWED boat (someone on board): the person on board presses CONFIRM on the onboard joystick within 10 s. The one that runs is lit; the other one switches straight over (REMOTE MANUAL <-> MANEUVER).

THERE IS NO RELEASE (an accidental release in the middle of a manoeuvre is dangerous): to end it, choose another mode - STANDBY (always), AUTO or DP (screen 2, with their own start rules). A copilot doesn't get these buttons. The gateway (licence, captain) and the AURIX (centred stick / CONFIRM, priorities, watchdogs) check every request again.

MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock): instead of the CDI three boxes REV | N | FWD - the lit one = the gear engaged now, the outlined one (thick) = what your stick asks for (a thin outline = a full deflection you are still holding, not asked yet). The throttle stays at idle.

OTHERWISE THE HUD ONLY SHOWS: no other button or key changes the driving; it sends only ACCEPT / REJECT answers, SAVE (video) and CLEAR SLOWDOWN (vision). THE LOGO: bottom right, above SAVE - small, never over an instrument or a warning. The same look as screen 2 (theme.py): the warning / caution colours are the same on both screens, dark / light switches both.

passages.heading: AR OVERLAYS (on the front video, button AR = menu, each one on / off):
passages.text: Horizon line + heel scale (pointer = heel, from the IMU), velocity vector (small circle with wings: where the boat really goes = course over ground; "drift 5 deg STBD"), waypoint diamond on the horizon with its distance (arrow at the edge when outside the picture), route ribbon on the water (fading with the distance), AIS ships boxed at their bearing (name, distance, CPA; red = threat; arrows at the edge for threats outside the picture), predicted path for 30 s and 60 s (speed + turn rate), water ahead shallower than the shallow limit tinted red (chart; no data = shallow), and the obstacle overlay of the camera detection (part N).

passages.heading: AR OVERLAYS (on the front video, button AR = menu, each one on / off):
passages.text: They need the CAMERA CALIBRATION in the gateway config: "vision": {"camera": {"height_m": 2.0, "tilt_down_deg": 2.0, "hfov_deg": 75, "vfov_deg": 44, "yaw_deg": 0}}

passages.heading: AR OVERLAYS (on the front video, button AR = menu, each one on / off):
passages.text: (height of the camera above the water, how far it looks down, field of view across / up-down, turned off the bow). Without it the HUD says "AR: camera calibration unknown" and shows no AR. Check it in harbour: the AR horizon must lie on the real horizon - else change tilt_down_deg. The AR is a picture help, NOT for navigation (chart / AIS / IMU errors).

passages.heading: AR OVERLAYS (on the front video, button AR = menu, each one on / off):
passages.text: SCREEN 1 ALSO SHOWS (the notices under the alarms): UNCREWED (blue: every CONFIRM on your joystick, a lost link stops the engine), LINK LOST (seconds to the engine kill, or "near the shore") / ENGINE KILLED, "MANEUVER: steering + gear only, throttle at idle", "boat not confirmed yet", NV DATA RESET (a stored setting was unusable: defaults in use - chapter 15) and NV FAULT (the data flash does not work: nothing is saved). In MANEUVER (and going astern in REMOTE / MANUAL) the two rear cameras are shown much bigger. A copilot's question for the captain appears here (YES / NO, lower part, chapter 5B "QUESTIONS").
The map IS screen 2 (chapter 5: "SCREEN 2 = THE MAP + FOUR CORNER PANELS", "EDITING ON THE MAP").

Shows depth chart, contours, sea marks, AIS ships, own boat (in the centre, turned with the heading) with its 6-minute course line, track, the route + waypoints (amber while edited / not sent), active waypoint, avoidance route, the geofence, a refused leg (red X), drift arrow, DR uncertainty circle, range rings with their distance; shallow-water / collision warnings as banners.
Layers View menu: depth, contours, sea marks, AIS, range rings (remembered).
Theme View menu: dark / light (both screens); NIGHT (screen 1, key N) = dim red on both maps.

passages.heading: BOTH WINDOWS (screen 1, screen 2) remember their monitor, place and size
passages.text: (groundstation\gs_layout.json) and come back there at the next start. Windows menu -> "Move the ... to monitor n", or Ctrl+Shift+1..9 in that window: the window goes to that monitor, maximised.

Like a cockpit, the PC speaks. DISPLAY ONLY: the sounds never change the driving. The boat's own BUZZER is separate: it sounds the boat's alarms by itself (also with no PC at all); this PC never switches it.

passages.heading: LEVELS
passages.text: WARNING urgent two-tone + voice, REPEATS until acknowledged on THIS PC (GENERAL WARNING lamp on the driver screen, ACK ALARM on screen 2, or Space / A on either screen). Can't be muted; never quieter than 60 %.

passages.heading: LEVELS
passages.text: CAUTION one chime + the voice once

passages.heading: LEVELS
passages.text: ADVISORY a soft click or a short voice (can be muted)

passages.heading: LEVELS
passages.text: FEEDBACK small sounds for your own actions (can be muted): camera shutter for SAVE, double chirp when the joystick takes over, confirm / refuse tones for the boat's answers, a question tone

passages.heading: LEVELS
passages.text: RULES: a higher level interrupts a lower one; two voices never at the same time (the next waits); the same callout is not repeated within 20 s (Sound tab); traffic is called only when a ship becomes a threat or gets worse; quiet / night mode = half volume, fewer advisories.

passages.heading: WHAT IT SAYS (texts: the "say." lines of the language files, chapter 5A)
passages.text: modes heading lock engaged, auto engaged, standby, joystick in control, remote driving engaged / ended

passages.heading: WHAT IT SAYS (texts: the "say." lines of the language files, chapter 5A)
passages.text: autopilot the "cavalry charge" when HDG LOCK / AUTO / REMOTE drops to STANDBY together with a fault (not when you press STANDBY)

Chosen because it is free, needs no internet, has a Greek voice (Windows only has one after installing a Greek speech pack) and also runs on the gateway PC. Install: chapter 3 g). Without Piper the ground station uses an installed Windows voice for that language, or tones only. Every callout is said as one sentence and all of them are made once in advance (groundstation\sound_cache\, not in git) so a callout starts at once; garbled takes are made again by themselves.

No Windows voice for the language = Piper speaks (the page says so). Piper now runs with calmer settings (less "wobble" at the start of a sentence) and every sentence starts with a short silence. A new voice or new settings: every phrase AND the guided tour are deleted and made again by themselves in the background (a few minutes the first time: tones only meanwhile).

The same from a command window: C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\python.exe tools\make_voice.py --samples C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\python.exe tools\make_voice.py (every phrase + tour now) OWN RECORDINGS: a WAV file groundstation\sounds\el\<key>.wav (or \en\) replaces the computer voice for that phrase, e.g. sounds\el\say.alarm.compass_lost.wav (groundstation\sounds\README.txt).

1. Open AURIX Development Studio, open the workspace with TRYGONS_C2. 2. Build: the hammer icon (sim/, groundstation/ and tools/ are excluded). 3. Flash and run: board on USB, Debug (bug icon), then Resume (F8). 4. Memory report after a build: C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\python.exe tools\mapreport.py "TriCore Debug (TASKING)\TRYGONS_C2.map" (the free TASKING licence only runs inside ADS: build there first.)

Expected memory (before the first ADS build; from the compiled objects + each core's stacks / CSA; iLLD + start-up code add a few KB on core 0): sh tools/check.sh (or: python tools\mapreport.py --objects <folder with .o>) core 0 RAM 119 KB of 240 KB (50 %) CPU1 RAM 12 KB of 240 KB ( 5 %: only the safety monitor + stacks) core 2 RAM 78 KB of 96 KB (81 %: logger + 1/4 of the black box) LMU blocks 0/1/2 54 KB of 64 KB each (84 %: 3/4 of the black box)
The 60 s black box (1200 records x 184 B = 216 KB) is split in 4 chunks: core 2's RAM + the three LMU blocks. CPU1's RAM must stay below 60 %: mapreport.py says FAIL (and the gate fails) above that.

Watchdogs are ON. When you stop the program in the debugger the watchdogs are paused too (normal for AURIX). If the board keeps resetting, the loop is too slow or stuck: look at the System tab and the log (EV_BOOT shows the reset reason).
For the first tests on the water the board steers, nothing else. The throttle and the gear stay with a person at the engine (by hand). Step-by-step checklist: FIRST_TEST.md.

passages.heading: SWITCH IT ON
passages.term: In Cpu0_Main.c remove the comment marks around
passages.text: In Cpu0_Main.c remove the comment marks around #define FIRST_TEST build (hammer) and flash. Put the comment back after the first tests. It can't be switched on or off from the PC (on purpose). FIRST_TEST is ON in git until the first boat tests are done - switch it off before testing throttle/gear.

passages.heading: WHAT IS DIFFERENT
passages.text: * Throttle and gear outputs are held safe: throttle servo = idle pulse, gear servo = neutral pulse, whatever happens (the servos may also be disconnected). * Power-up needs NO joystick, NO neutral switch and NO gateway. * Only STANDBY, TRAINING and HEADING LOCK (plus the BENCH TEST on the dock, chapter 6B - it never drives the throttle or the gear). MANUAL (joystick), AUTO and remote driving are refused ("not possible in this mode").

passages.heading: WHAT IS DIFFERENT
passages.text: * HEADING LOCK and TRAINING steer only while the GPS says the boat moves AHEAD (at least 2 kn, course within 60 deg of the heading). Stopped or going astern: the steering rests. * TRAINING: drive slowly by hand (like its own 20 % throttle, ~4-5 kn). Faster, the boat turns too far and TRAINING stops itself.

passages.heading: WHAT IS DIFFERENT
passages.text: * Take over: the STANDBY button or the EMERGENCY STOP (and the person at the throttle). Every other safety rule stays active. * Shown: a big magenta banner on the ground station "FIRST TEST - STEERING ONLY", and in the telemetry (TELEM2 group I).

passages.heading: EMERGENCY STOP (every configuration, not only the first test)
passages.text: A mushroom switch. Pressed: STANDBY at once, alarm EMERGENCY STOP, and nothing but STANDBY works until it is released. Its hard-wired contacts stop the ENGINE through the kill circuit in EVERY profile (CREWED too) and cut the DP thrusters' contactor. It does NOT cut the servo power (the DroneCAN servo nodes stay powered); its second contact tells the board (WIRING.md).

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.text: A mode for checking the wiring with the boat on the trailer or tied up, engine OFF (FIRST_TEST.md part 3). Ground station, tab "Bench".

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHO / WHEN
passages.text: * Only the laptop on the USB cable (never through the gateway / from shore: "not allowed"). * Only from STANDBY, not while the GPS says the boat moves (> 1.5 kn), not with the emergency stop pressed. Works in the normal and the FIRST TEST build. * Throttle idle + gear neutral all the time.

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHAT IT DOES
passages.text: * Shows every sensor live (10 times a second): IMU (heading, yaw rate, roll / pitch, acceleration, compass accuracy 0-3), GPS (fix, satellites, SOG / COG, spoofing and jamming states), motor current, limit switches, emergency stop, SD card, UART errors.

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHAT IT DOES
passages.text: * << LEFT / RIGHT >>: the steering motor runs 100, 200 or 300 ms. At most one pulse every 0.2 s; never past the estimated maximum angle; refused toward an end stop whose switch is open ("at the end stop").

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHAT IT DOES
passages.text: * Panel buttons: each press is shown (green box + count). They do nothing else - except STANDBY, which ends the bench test as always. * Buzzer test 1 s. * Servo outputs: the throttle and gear pulse widths being sent (idle / neutral), to compare with a scope or a servo tester.

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHAT IT DOES
passages.text: * Stack use (under the sensors): for core 0, CPU1 and core 2 the deepest use of the user stack and of the interrupt stack since the power-up, "used / reserved B (%)". "?" = still measuring (about 2 s). Amber = less than 50 % margin, red = OVERFLOW (the stack reached its end): stop and report. On the PC simulator the numbers are simulated (it says so). Display only - it changes nothing on the boat.

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: WHAT IT DOES
passages.text: * Monitor trip test (asks first): the CPU1 safety monitor trips for real - idle + neutral forced by the monitor itself, steering held, engine kill circuit opened (UNCREWED only), buzzer, STANDBY, alarm MONITOR TRIP. It stays until the board is powered off and on (that is the point: nothing can undo it).

passages.chapter: BENCH TEST: EVERY SENSOR AND OUTPUT ON THE DOCK
passages.heading: IT ENDS BY ITSELF (back to STANDBY, reason "bench test ended")
passages.text: 10 min without a bench command, the USB cable unplugged (3 s), HELM taken by another station, the boat moving. Also: STANDBY button, emergency stop, any fault, the joystick moved (-> MANUAL, normal build).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: STANDBY engine idle, neutral, steering held. Power-up and after faults.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: MANUAL the joystick: stick left/right = outboard angle (full range), forward/back = throttle ahead/astern (centre = idle + neutral). Gear changes always go idle -> neutral -> gear, however fast you move the stick.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: HDG LOCK press HDG LOCK on the panel: the autopilot holds the heading the boat has now. -1/+1/-10/+10 (panel or PC) change it. The throttle stays on the stick (ahead and astern) - you stay in HDG LOCK. In reverse the outboard is held straight. Moving the stick sideways takes over (MANUAL). With people on board (CREWED) only the panel button starts it - never the PC. UNCREWED HDG LOCK (owner 2026-11-01): nobody on board, so the captain at the shore holding HELM (with the licence) chooses HDG LOCK on screen 2 ("HDG LOCK" in the control panel) - ONLY while REMOTE MANUAL or MANEUVER runs, with the shore stick centred (the lever may stay where it is).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: It starts at once (no CONFIRM) and locks the heading the boat has at that moment; +-1 / +-10 come from the station. THE THROTTLE: it stays at what it was when you switched (never more than the REMOTE limit of 20 %; from MANEUVER: idle) and can only come DOWN. The TWCS lever is a ceiling: pull it back and the boat slows down; push it forward again and it goes back up to the value it held - never above it. The lever never changes gear and never reverses. To get more power choose REMOTE MANUAL again. A station without a lever (stick Y as the throttle): the held value only.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: What still acts (like in AUTO, but only by slowing down - it NEVER steers): shallow water / the shore ahead (slows down; closer than 100 m = STOP: idle + neutral until you choose another mode), an AIS ship on a collision course (slows down; no avoidance turn, no proposal), the camera obstacle detection (only if its stage 3 is ON). Outside the geofence: STANDBY (idle + neutral first) + alarm GEOFENCE. Shore joystick data older than 0.3 s: idle + neutral at once, STANDBY after 5 s (as in REMOTE). Compass lost: STANDBY. The lost-link rules are the usual ones (near the shore always 3 s, chapter 9 B).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: A copilot asking for HDG LOCK = a question on the captain's screen 1 (ACCEPT); STANDBY is always free. NO DATA = SHALLOW (step 13q2d): HDG LOCK is refused (like an AUTO start, code 114 / 6) when the gateway has no position, no depth charts, a position too uncertain (more than 100 m), or shallow water / the shore closer than 100 m ahead, and when the GPS is not trusted. If the charts, the position or the shore data from the gateway are lost while it runs: STOP (idle + neutral, alarm SHALLOW WATER) - the boat checks this itself, even if the gateway still answers.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: GPS lost / suspect while it runs: like AUTO - it carries on by dead reckoning with the held throttle cut to 70 %; dead reckoning too uncertain (200 m) or longer than 10 min: STANDBY (idle + neutral first) + alarm. THE GATEWAY'S LOOK-AHEAD IS REQUIRED (step 13q2e): HDG LOCK is also refused (code 6) while the gateway's navigation check is not running (no fresh navigation request) and when the shore / shallow water is 100 m or closer in any direction.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: While it runs: the gateway's navigation check stops arriving for 3 s (gateway fault, link trouble) = STOP (idle + neutral, alarm DRIVER DECISION) - with nobody on board the boat never carries on without the look-ahead (AUTO keeps its old rule: hold the heading at 4 kn). The shore / shallow water 100 m or closer in any direction (also beside or behind) = STOP (alarm SHALLOW WATER). The STOP lasts until you choose another mode.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: STEERING BY HAND IN HDG LOCK (step 13q3, owner 2026-10-31): move the shore stick sideways (more than 15 %) and the boat turns with it, like REMOTE (same steering speed) - HDG LOCK stays, the throttle stays as it is (screen 1 / 2: "MANUAL STEERING - HDG LOCK waiting"). Let the stick go: 2 s later the boat turns back to the OLD locked heading. To keep the new course press the stick's TRIGGER (shore_joystick.json "trigger_button", default stick button 1) while you steer (or within the 2 s after letting go): the heading at that moment becomes the locked heading ("NEW HEADING 245°" for 3 s, the mark on the heading tape moves).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: The trigger does nothing when you are not steering, and nothing while a question waits for your answer. One press never does two things (step 13q3b): the trigger is also ignored when it comes with the CONFIRM button or within 0.5 s after a CONFIRM press, and a trigger mapped to the same button as CONFIRM / SAVE in shore_joystick.json is never sent (the Remote page says so) - give it a button of its own. Shore stick data lost while you steer = the 0.3 s rule above. Every start / end / new heading / stop of steering by hand is written to the boat's black box (log event 26 SOVR).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: AUTO a waypoint program (up to 50 waypoints). Each waypoint has a leg speed, an arrival radius and an action: continue / slow down / stop in neutral. At the end: stop + alarm (or hold the heading slowly). AUTO starts only with the PC "AUTO START" AND the joystick CONFIRM within 10 s (stick centred). Pause, resume (+ CONFIRM) and skip from the PC. Line following, speed control, rough-water slow-down, dead reckoning without GPS, GPS integrity check: all as before. AUTO RETURN ("Return" in the control panel of screen 2): the boat drives the program BACKWARDS from the leg it is on to waypoint 1 and stops there in neutral (STANDBY + ARRIVED).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: Each leg back at the speed of that leg, the waypoints keep their slow / stop actions. Like AUTO START it needs the joystick CONFIRM within 10 s (stick centred; UNCREWED: the shore joystick) - from STANDBY, HDG LOCK, MANUAL (stick centred) or AUTO itself (running, paused, stopped, finished). NEVER out of REMOTE MANUAL / MANEUVER (refused, code 7): the captain driving by hand chooses AUTO START or another mode. The copilot may ask for it WITHOUT the captain's ACCEPT (like AUTO pause) - except while the captain drives in REMOTE / MANEUVER: then it is a question on screen 1.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: The gateway checks the way back like a route: shallow water (114), the geofence (120); only a program the gateway checked itself (uploaded through it) can be driven back (121 otherwise: upload it again). The stored program is not changed: AUTO START afterwards drives it forward from waypoint 1 again; a new upload ends the return. The joystick still wins (MANUAL; RESUME + CONFIRM goes on back).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: STEERING BY HAND IN AUTO - UNCREWED (step 13q3, owner 2026-10-31: "In AUTO I can always drive by hand, except throttle up; to stop AUTO totally I choose another mode"): the HELM captain moves the shore stick sideways (more than 15 %) and steers by hand with the REMOTE steering speed; AUTO stays the mode and keeps its speed (screen 1 / 2: "MANUAL STEERING - AUTO waiting"). Your steering wins over a collision avoidance turn while you hold the stick (the speed limits of the gateway still slow the boat). Let the stick go: 2 s later AUTO steers again and comes back to the line to the active waypoint (like after an avoidance turn).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: Steering out of the geofence by hand = STANDBY + alarm GEOFENCE (while AUTO steers itself the geofence is its route check). Shore stick data older than 0.3 s while you steer by hand = idle + neutral at once, the heading held, alarm REMOTE DRIVING LINK LOST, STANDBY after 5 s (never back by itself); while you do not steer, AUTO does not need the stick.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: WHILE YOU STEER AUTO BY HAND the boat protects itself like in UNCREWED HDG LOCK (step 13q3b): your course was never checked like AUTO's route, so the boat STOPS (idle + neutral) when the shore / shallow water is 100 m or closer (alarm SHALLOW WATER), when the gateway has no chart / position data or the position is too uncertain, when the gateway's navigation check stops arriving (alarm DRIVER DECISION), when the GPS is not trusted, or when the gateway asks to stop. You keep steering by hand; let the stick go and AUTO steers again - at idle. The STOP lasts until you choose a mode again (AUTO START, REMOTE ...).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: While AUTO steers itself nothing of this changes. A new HELM captain (role swap) never steers on with the old override: it ends at the swap and his stick must be seen centred first; the old captain's lever limit stays until the new captain moves his lever. THE TWCS LEVER IN AUTO (UNCREWED) = a power CEILING: it only takes power away, never adds. At the AUTO start it is in neutral and does nothing yet. It starts limiting when you PULL IT BACK (a real move down from where it was) - then it limits at once: in the neutral zone or further back = idle, AUTO steers at idle (still in forward gear).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: Pushing it up past AUTO's throttle engages it too. While the lever is below the throttle but not engaged yet, both screens say "The lever does not limit the power yet - move it" with the lever position where it meets the throttle. Pulled back = less power, the reverse zone = idle too - the lever never changes gear or mode. Pushed fully forward = AUTO's own throttle again (never more). The same in UNCREWED HDG LOCK (above). With people on board (CREWED) nothing changes: the onboard joystick takes full MANUAL at once, the shore stick does nothing in AUTO / HDG LOCK.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: TRAINING outboard calibration, started from STANDBY by the PC.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: Mode changes allowed (all others are refused and logged): from \ to STANDBY MANUAL HDG_LOCK AUTO TRAINING REMOTE MANEUVER STANDBY - yes yes yes yes yes yes MANUAL yes - yes yes no no no HDG_LOCK yes yes - yes no yes no AUTO yes yes yes - no yes no TRAINING yes yes no no - no no REMOTE yes yes yes* yes no - yes MANEUVER yes yes yes* yes no yes -

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: (REMOTE = REMOTE MANUAL, the shore joystick, chapter 9 part D; MANEUVER = steering + gear at idle for the dock / trailer, chapter 7A; REMOTE / MANEUVER -> AUTO with the AUTO start rules (request + CONFIRM), -> DP (not in the table above) only at idle, in neutral and slow, with the DP start rules; * -> HDG LOCK directly ONLY UNCREWED, by the shore HELM captain (owner 2026-11-01, see HDG LOCK above); CREWED: STANDBY first, then the panel HDG LOCK button)

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: MODES
passages.text: Extra rules: only the joystick enters MANUAL; MANUAL is left only with the stick centred; AUTO needs compass, GPS, a valid program and CONFIRM; TRAINING only from STANDBY by the PC; nothing but STANDBY until the outputs are armed (chapter 12).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE JOYSTICK ALWAYS WINS (analog or USB - the rules are the same; the USB lever has a few extra ones, chapter 8)
passages.text: * Take over from ANY mode: stick sideways past 15 % for 0.1 s, forward / back (not in HDG LOCK, where that is the throttle), or TAKE. Chirp. An AUTO program is suspended (resume later: PC + CONFIRM). * Give back: CENTRE the stick, then joystick AUTO (back to HDG LOCK if that was interrupted, otherwise STANDBY) or panel HDG LOCK. Not centred: refused + chirp. The PC can't take control from the stick.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE JOYSTICK ALWAYS WINS (analog or USB - the rules are the same; the USB lever has a few extra ones, chapter 8)
passages.text: * CONFIRM only answers a request from the PC (AUTO start / resume, power raise). It counts only with the stick centred and the joystick armed. Nothing pending: nothing happens. It never changes the mode by itself. While a CONFIRM is pending and the stick that must confirm is not centred (the onboard stick; a CREWED MANEUVER: also the captain's shore stick - both sticks centred; UNCREWED: the captain's shore stick and the lever at neutral) both screens show "Centre the joystick to confirm" (screen 1 notices, screen 2 message line; display only, W79).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE JOYSTICK ALWAYS WINS (analog or USB - the rules are the same; the USB lever has a few extra ones, chapter 8)
passages.text: * At power-up the stick must be centred, otherwise it is ignored and the outputs stay off (alarm) until you let go. * Broken wire while it drives: idle, neutral, STANDBY; the gyro holds the course until idle + neutral, then the steering stops.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE STANDBY BUTTON ALWAYS WINS
passages.text: Every mode -> STANDBY (idle + neutral first, then steering held). The throttle is commanded to IDLE AT ONCE in STANDBY (no rate limit, step 11e; normal driving, a lowered power limit and a planned arrival stop come down at thr_dn_pc_s, 50 %/s). The gear goes to neutral once the throttle servo must be at idle (thr_trav_s, the worst-case 6 s from full). Until idle + neutral is reached the boat is still steered:

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE STANDBY BUTTON ALWAYS WINS
passages.text: * from MANUAL: your stick keeps steering the outboard (even if you still hold it), then the steering stops; * from REMOTE MANUAL: the shore stick is ignored at once, the gyro holds the course; * from HDG LOCK / AUTO: the heading is held (gyro if the compass is gone).

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: THE STANDBY BUTTON ALWAYS WINS
passages.text: A stick that is still held can't take control back until it was centred. While the stick is held, nothing else can be engaged either: the HDG LOCK button is refused (short chirp), AUTO start / resume, remote driving and TRAINING are refused with "centre the joystick". Let go of the stick (centre), then engage. The PC can't override the button. In STANDBY the button acknowledges alarms.

passages.chapter: HOW THE BOAT BEHAVES: MODES, BUTTONS, JOYSTICK
passages.heading: AUTO PROGRAM - HOW TO
passages.text: 1. Program tab: add waypoints (or tick "click adds" and click the map), set leg speed, radius, action; choose the end action. 2. "Upload to boat". The boat checks it (coordinates, number <= 50, leg length 10 m .. 50 km, speeds within the maximum, radius 5..500 m) and stores it with a checksum (kept after power-off). 3. Raise the power limit if you want more than ~7 kn (chapter 10). 4. AUTO START, then CONFIRM on the joystick within 10 s.

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: CREWED an onboard joystick (analog, or T.16000M + TWCS through the Teensy) was found at power-up and passed its self-check. Everything works as in chapter 7: the onboard joystick wins, every CONFIRM is pressed on the onboard joystick.

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: UNCREWED no onboard joystick at power-up (or it failed its self-check within 6 s). The onboard joystick is ignored completely: no MANUAL, no CONFIRM, no joystick buttons; the panel HDG LOCK and course buttons do nothing (nobody is on board). HDG LOCK comes only from the shore captain, out of REMOTE / MANEUVER, with the throttle held and only lowered (chapter 7, HDG LOCK). Every CONFIRM (power raise, AUTO start / resume / return, DP) is pressed on the shore captain's joystick instead: same rules - stick centred, within 10 s, only for a pending request.

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: REMOTE MANUAL and MANEUVER need NO CONFIRM here (owner 2026-10-31): the captain's choice starts them at once, only with the shore stick centred and the lever at neutral at that moment.

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: Both profiles: the STANDBY button and the emergency stop always work. The profile is shown on every screen and in the log. It changes only in STANDBY with the boat stopped, and only one way: a joystick plugged in on board (and passing its self-check for 10 s) makes an UNCREWED boat CREWED. A CREWED boat whose joystick fails or is unplugged stays CREWED (that is a JOYSTICK FAULT: idle + neutral, STANDBY, alarm). UNCREWED needs a power-up without the joystick. A joystick that appears while an UNCREWED boat is driving is a fault: STANDBY + alarm PROFILE CHANGED.

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: After every profile change the power limit is back at 30 % / 5 % and the outputs re-arm (CREWED: stick centred).

passages.heading: THE PROFILE (decided by the boat, never by a PC)
passages.text: OPERATING RULE: UNPLUG THE ONBOARD JOYSTICK BEFORE ANY UNCREWED OPERATION, and check that every screen shows UNCREWED before the boat leaves the dock. With someone on board: joystick plugged in, CREWED. The FIRST TEST build (chapter 6A) is always CREWED.

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: * Steering and gear only: the captain's joystick sideways = outboard angle; the GEAR is on the STICK (owner 2026-10-31, step 13q5): - stick fully FORWARD and held ~0.3 s = FORWARD, - stick in the CENTRE (let go: it springs back) = NEUTRAL at once,

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: - stick fully BACK and held ~0.3 s = REVERSE. A short flick asks nothing; half way asks nothing; pulling the other way than the gear asked = NEUTRAL at once (then hold it for the other gear). The ~0.3 s is counted on WHEN THE STATION SENT the stick positions, not on when they reached the boat: a packet delayed on the network never makes a short flick look like a hold (step 13q5c). Just after MANEUVER starts, before the first stick packet arrives, the gear goes to NEUTRAL. The TWCS throttle lever is NOT used in MANEUVER (it must be at neutral to start). The throttle is ALWAYS at idle - no rpm control at all.

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: The station sends the stick's Y axis beside the lever (shore_joystick.json "stick_y", default: the stick's own Y; check on the Tools page "Remote" that pushing the stick forward shows + on the line "stick fwd / back (sent)" - a wrong sign would ask REVERSE with the stick forward; in MANEUVER the line "boat sees:" shows what the boat received: "full FORWARD (+) -> gear F" - step 13q5b). Because of that, every "stick centred" check (REMOTE / MANEUVER start, CONFIRM, HDG LOCK) also needs the stick's forward / back centred.

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: * Gear changes go idle -> neutral -> gear, as always; FORWARD <-> REVERSE always through NEUTRAL with its wait. The AURIX refuses anything unsafe. * MANEUVER -> HDG LOCK (UNCREWED): the stick must be centred (sideways AND forward / back - also at a station without a TWCS lever, step 13q5c; else "centre the joystick"), so the gear is NEUTRAL by then - HDG LOCK ALWAYS starts in neutral at idle (also when the gear had not shifted out of forward yet; step 13q5b).

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: * Start: button MANEUVER (DOCK / TRAILER) on the captain's station (it must hold HELM and the user must hold a manual licence). CREWED: then CONFIRM on the onboard joystick within 10 s - the boat takes that CONFIRM only while the captain's shore stick is centred (sideways AND forward / back) and its data is fresh (else a short chirp, nothing changes; centre the shore stick and press CONFIRM again within the 10 s; step WB). UNCREWED: at once, only with the captain's stick centred and the lever at neutral. From STANDBY or REMOTE MANUAL (and back to REMOTE MANUAL the same way).

passages.heading: MANEUVER (trailer, ramp, dock approach) - captain only
passages.text: * Ends: another mode chosen (STANDBY, AUTO, DP - there is no RELEASE), STANDBY button, the onboard joystick (CREWED), any fault, HELM lost. Joystick data old / missing: neutral + course held, STANDBY after 5 s (as REMOTE MANUAL). While the generator runs (chapter 7, GENERATOR) an UNCREWED start is refused: switch it off first. * Not in the FIRST TEST build.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: Lost link = no working link to the captain's (HELM) shore station on any channel for the LINK TIME (below, 3 s unless the captain set more): the gateway measures how long it has not heard the HELM station and tells the AURIX once a second; the gateway itself lost (3 s) or nobody holding HELM any more (also a RELEASE of HELM - hand over with the role swap instead, chapter 9) count at once. LINK TIME ("max time without connection", owner 2026-10-31): screen 2, panel "Control", the geofence line, buttons - / + (3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60 s). Only the captain holding HELM can change it (a copilot gets "captain only").

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: It is kept in the AURIX's memory for THIS session only: back to 3 s when the ground station is restarted, when HELM changes (another station, a role swap, HELM taken again after a drop) and after every AURIX reset. While it is above 3 s both screens show "LINK TIME 30 s (OVERRIDE)" all the time. It is NEVER used near the shore (closer than 50 m, or no shore information): there it is always 3 s ("not in force now"). REMOTE MANUAL keeps its own 0.3 s joystick-data check (neutral at once, STANDBY after 5 s) whatever the LINK TIME. Use it for a known short outage at open sea (e.g.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: Starlink changing satellites); the boat goes on with what it was doing (AUTO, DP) for that long without anyone watching it.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: 1. Always first: STANDBY - throttle to idle, neutral (fast closing rate), alarm LINK LOST. 2. Near the shore (closer than near_shore_m, default 50 m, to the shallow-water / shore data the route check uses) - or the gateway gives no valid / fresh shore distance: ENGINE KILL as soon as idle + neutral.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: 3. Open sea: wait lostlink_grace_s (default 10 s). Link back in time: the boat stays in STANDBY at idle / neutral and the station sees the alarm (it never drives on by itself). Otherwise: ENGINE KILL. The longest the engine runs without a link: LINK TIME + 10 s.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: A killed engine stays killed (alarm ENGINE KILLED) until the AURIX is POWER CYCLED ON BOARD (a real power-off / power-on; a watchdog reset or a software reset of the AURIX keeps the kill) OR the HELM station sends RESTART (Tools -> Engine; next part: throttle idle, gear in neutral and the e-stop released are checked on the boat). A CREWED boat never kills the engine: it keeps the behaviour of chapter 9 (REMOTE LINK LOST, HELM to nobody, no mode change by itself). near_shore_m (50 m, owner 2026-10-31; never below 50) and lostlink_grace_s are parameters (Config tab) - the grace time is still TO CONFIRM.

passages.heading: LOST LINK (UNCREWED ONLY) AND THE ENGINE KILL
passages.text: The kill relay itself is not chosen yet (WIRING.md 3A): no uncrewed operation before it is fitted and tested.

passages.heading: THE MANUAL LICENCE
passages.text: Each user in the gateway's user database may have "licence": true (a manual / boat driving licence). Only such a user can ask for REMOTE MANUAL or MANEUVER; others get "no manual licence" (code 116). Add it with: python3 users.py add NAME HELM licence

passages.heading: THE ACADEMY LEVELS (menu Academy on the ground station)
passages.text: The academy keeps training accounts on the SHORE PC: OBSERVER -> DRIVER -> CAPTAIN, an expiry, and a logbook (lessons, scores, attempts, exams, driving hours). Only CAPTAIN gives the manual licence; an expired level counts as OBSERVER. Menu Academy -> "Open the academy" opens it in its OWN window. It only ever uses the simulator or recordings - never this station's boat link. The banner "TRAINING - SIMULATION" is always at its top. How a level reaches the boat:

passages.heading: THE ACADEMY LEVELS (menu Academy on the ground station)
passages.text: 1. Academy window: "Academy key" once (copied to the clipboard). Put the same text into the gateway's secrets.json as "academy_key" (never in git). 2. Academy window: the level (from the practical test - see below), then "Make the gateway file".

passages.heading: THE ACADEMY LEVELS (menu Academy on the ground station)
passages.text: 3. Ground station logged in to the gateway: menu Academy -> "Send the academy levels to the gateway" (HELM users only). The gateway checks the signature, ignores users it doesn't know (it never makes a new user), keeps its last copy on its SSD (used when the academy can't be reached) and uses the level at the NEXT LOGIN only - a station already logged in keeps its licence (never taken away mid-trip). A user without an academy level keeps the "licence" flag of secrets.json. Backup: "Backup" copies the accounts + logbook to a folder you choose (a second shore PC or a USB disk; never a boat's gateway). The key is not copied - keep it safe separately.

passages.heading: THE GUIDED TOUR (menu Academy -> Guided tour)
passages.text: A tour of everything on the station, one item at a time: screen 1 (every HUD box and button), screen 2 (the map and every corner panel), every page of the tools window, every mode, every alarm with its level, the MASTER lamps, the joystick and the panel buttons. Screen 1, screen 2 and the tools pages are REAL screenshots of the ground station (made from the demo); the item explained is framed in amber at its real place and the rest of the picture is dimmed. The modes, alarms, lamps, joystick and panel buttons are shown as drawings.

passages.heading: THE GUIDED TOUR (menu Academy -> Guided tour)
passages.text: (For the picture of screen 1 every button of the bottom bar is shown, also CLEAR SLOWDOWN / RESTORE POWER, which appear on the boat only in their situations.) After a change of the screens the pictures are made again by python tools/demo_screens.py --tour (tools/check.sh does it by itself when the layout changed; it stops and restarts the demo). Next / Back (or the arrow keys, space = next), the chapter list on the left jumps, "Say again" repeats the voice, "Voice: ON / OFF". The Greek voice is a RECORDED narration (academy/tour_voice/el, Opus; it needs ffmpeg, which the demo uses too); a step without a recording, or whose text was changed after the recording, uses the offline voice.

passages.heading: THE GUIDED TOUR (menu Academy -> Guided tour)
passages.text: The English voice is the offline voice. The offline voice (Piper) is made by this station's offline voice (Piper) in the background the first time you open the tour from the menu - a few minutes; until then the tour shows the text only. The academy window's "Guided tour" button opens the same tour. TOUR.bat (next to START_DEMO.bat, double-click) opens the tour on its own in Greek - no demo, no boat, no gateway needed. The tour only explains: it never connects to a boat (banner at the top).

passages.heading: SIMULATOR LESSONS (academy window -> "Simulator lessons")
passages.text: Hands-on lessons on the SIMULATOR of this PC - never a boat (banner at the top). Press "Start the simulator" (or have sim/autopilot_sim server 5760 running), pick a lesson (grouped by level) and press Start. You drive with the simulated panel buttons, the joystick pad (drag the knob; it springs back to the centre when you let go, unless "Hold the stick" is ticked), TAKE / CONFIRM (held while pressed) and the PC buttons (ask for a code, raise, lower the limit, acknowledge). Every step is checked from the simulated boat itself, not from your clicks; a hint shows after a while; a step with a time limit (e.g.

passages.heading: SIMULATOR LESSONS (academy window -> "Simulator lessons")
passages.text: the STANDBY reaction) fails when you are too late - press Retry. Lessons: HDG LOCK + course changes, joystick takeover + hand-back, STANDBY always wins, reacting to an alarm (DRIVER), raising the power limit with the code + CONFIRM (CAPTAIN). Select your account in the academy window first: the results go to your logbook (lessons passed = required before the exam); without one it is practice.

passages.heading: QUIZZES (academy window -> "Quizzes")
passages.text: Pick question pools (none = all) and start. Multiple choice, picture questions (click the asked part on a drawing of the screen) and alarm sounds (which level is it?). Random order, the explanation after every answer, the score per pool in your logbook (pools under 70 % show as weak areas in the instructor view). The alarm sounds are the station's own tones: they are prepared when you open the academy from the station's menu; without them the sound questions are left out (the window says so).

passages.heading: EMERGENCY SCENARIOS (academy window -> "Emergency scenarios")
passages.text: Emergencies on the SIMULATOR of this PC (same inputs as the lessons). A scenario first sets up a normal trip (e.g. HDG LOCK at speed), then something goes wrong - you are NOT told what to do: react as on the boat.
