Your reaction time is measured from the moment the emergency starts; full marks within the scenario's time, fewer points the later you react, failed when too late, when you do something dangerous (e.g. a turn to port in front of a ship from starboard) or when the boat gets too close to the hazard / runs aground.

passages.heading: EMERGENCY SCENARIOS (academy window -> "Emergency scenarios")
passages.text: The ten scenarios: compass failure, GPS spoofing, slamming, joystick fault, power raise refused, a ship on a collision course (AIS), shallow water ahead, a swimmer / kayak near the beach (no AIS!), gateway lost, remote link lost. Compass, GPS, slamming, joystick and the refusal are REAL faults of the simulated boat (it reacts with its own safety rules); the ship, the shallows, the swimmer and the gateway / remote-link alarms are drawn by the academy in its small picture of the station (map, AIS list, depth, forward camera) - the academy never plays the gateway.

passages.heading: EMERGENCY SCENARIOS (academy window -> "Emergency scenarios")
passages.text: At the end: the debrief (result, reaction time, closest approach, the right action, why) and "Replay" (the recorded track with a time slider; the file is kept in academy/data/replays). Results with the reaction time go to your logbook.

passages.heading: VIDEO LESSONS FROM REAL TRIPS (academy window -> "Video lessons")
passages.text: Lessons made from the boat's SAVED EVENTS (the SAVE recordings that the sync brings to the shore PC): the camera picture of a real trip with the station's HUD redrawn over it from the trip's log, in step with the video (switch cameras with the buttons under the picture, HUD on / off). The video stops at the decision points: a DECISION question (pick what you do) or SPOT THE HAZARD (click on the danger in the picture). After every answer the explanation; at the end the score (70 % to pass) goes to your logbook.

passages.heading: VIDEO LESSONS FROM REAL TRIPS (academy window -> "Video lessons")
passages.text: The lessons play only their own small trimmed copies, with faces and number plates blurred - never a live camera, never a boat (banner at the top). LESSON EDITOR (academy window -> "Lesson editor", for the instructor):

passages.heading: VIDEO LESSONS FROM REAL TRIPS (academy window -> "Video lessons")
passages.text: 1. "Open a saved event..." -> the event.json in the synced folder video/events/<event>/ (its log is found by itself; a log without GPS time = video only, no HUD). 2. Move the cursor (picture of the chosen camera at that moment), "Start here" / "End here" = the clip (3 s .. 10 min). Tick the cameras for the lesson and the main one.

passages.heading: VIDEO LESSONS FROM REAL TRIPS (academy window -> "Video lessons")
passages.text: 3. Questions at the cursor: fill in the question + explanation in Greek AND English. Decision: the choices separated by ";" (the same number in both languages) + the number of the right one -> "Add decision point". Hazard: draw the area(s) on the picture (Box = hazard area) -> "Add hazard question".

passages.heading: VIDEO LESSONS FROM REAL TRIPS (academy window -> "Video lessons")
passages.text: 4. Blur: Box = blur area, draw it over a face / number plate; it is blurred from the cursor for the given seconds (list "Blur areas"). Check every person and number plate in the clip. 5. Title (Greek + English), level, "Make lesson": the small copies (640 px wide, no sound, blurred) + the HUD data go to academy/data/videolessons/ <id>/ on THIS PC (never into git). The original event stays untouched. The video lessons stay on the PC where they were made (copy the folder academy/data/videolessons to another shore PC to use them there).

passages.heading: EXAMS (academy window -> "Exams")
passages.text: One exam per level: the DRIVER exam (for an OBSERVER) and the CAPTAIN exam (for a valid DRIVER). Select your account first. The required simulator lessons must be passed before. 15 questions from the quiz pools, random order; the answers are NOT shown during the exam, only the score at the end (pass mark 80 %). Starting an exam counts as an attempt; after 3 failed attempts the next one waits 24 hours. PASSING AN EXAM NEVER CHANGES YOUR LEVEL - the level goes up only with the PRACTICAL TEST on the boat.

passages.heading: LOGINS AND 2FA (academy window -> "Log in", "Password", "2FA app")
passages.text: Every account can have a password (at least 8 characters). CAPTAIN and instructor accounts also need a 6-digit code from an OFFLINE authenticator app on the phone (no SMS): "2FA app" with the password shows the key and copies the otpauth link - type it into the app. 5 wrong logins = locked for 10 minutes. The passwords and 2FA keys stay on this PC (academy/data/auth/), never in a backup: after restoring a backup, set them again. The instructor actions need the instructor's login: renew, supervise an online session, certificate, and (after the first set-up) set a level.

passages.heading: LEVELS GO UP ONLY WITH THE PRACTICAL TEST
passages.text: "Set level" in the academy window can only LOWER a level once an instructor with a valid CAPTAIN level exists (before that, during the first set-up, it sets the first levels). OBSERVER -> DRIVER -> CAPTAIN only through the practical test on the boat (below). Nothing done online raises a level.

passages.heading: RENEWAL AND CURRENCY
passages.text: A level is valid 12 months (a reminder 30 days before). Renewal (the instructor presses "Renew" for the selected account): DRIVER = within the last 90 days a refresher simulator lesson + a quiz (70 %) + one emergency scenario; CAPTAIN = the same + a practical check ride every 24 months. Expired more than 3 months = the full practical test again. An expired level counts as OBSERVER. Currency: no logged driving for 90 days -> the gateway file carries the level WITHOUT the captain's licence until a supervised refresher trip on the boat (a CAPTAIN on board approves + the onboard CONFIRM).

passages.heading: THE ONLINE ACADEMY
passages.text: The academy runs only on the academy PC on shore (never on a boat's gateway). Trainees reach it from home with a remote desktop / SSH over Tailscale; the Tailscale rules let a trainee's device reach ONLY the academy PC, never a boat (example in academy/online.py; check yours with online.check_acl). In an online session (shown under the banner) exams are allowed only while an instructor marked the session supervised ("Supervise online session", 10..480 minutes), and nothing online raises a level.

passages.heading: CERTIFICATE (academy window -> "Certificate PDF", instructor)
passages.text: A one-page PDF for the selected account: the level IN FORCE and its expiry, the practical test, the exams passed, lessons / scenarios, driving hours and currency. An expired level is printed as NOT IN FORCE. Logged.

passages.heading: THE PRACTICAL TEST ON THE BOAT (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test on THIS boat")
passages.text: This is the only academy part that sees a real boat - and it only WATCHES (the telemetry this station receives + its event log) and grades. It never sends anything that drives: every safety rule stays the boat's own. CREWED profile only; the examiner (a valid CAPTAIN, his own login + 2FA, never the trainee) sits at the station on board.

passages.heading: THE PRACTICAL TEST ON THE BOAT (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test on THIS boat")
passages.text: 1. Examiner logs in; trainee, kind: practical test (one level up), check ride (CAPTAIN, every 24 months) or supervised refresher trip. 2. Type the wind (kn + the direction it comes FROM), tick: calm water, examiner on board, the wind is right. "Check" shows everything that is missing: test area set (never the placeholder) and the boat inside it, STANDBY, start power limit 30 / 5 %, calm water (sea state + slamming monitor), wind <= 12 kn and not strong (>= 8 kn) from the north or from the right side of the ramp, 08:00-19:00, the exam of the level passed + the lessons, fresh telemetry.

passages.heading: THE PRACTICAL TEST ON THE BOAT (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test on THIS boat")
passages.text: Then "Start" (the whole ride is recorded in academy/data/practical/ and linked to the logbook).

passages.heading: THE PRACTICAL TEST ON THE BOAT (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test on THIS boat")
passages.text: 3. Tasks: leave the harbour, HDG LOCK + a course change of 10 deg, joystick takeover + hand-back, the examiner's ALARM (shown on this screen only - the trainee must put the boat in STANDBY within 15 s), return, and for CAPTAIN the trailer approach + loading in MANEUVER (requested and confirmed the normal way). A task is first SEEN in the telemetry, then the examiner approves it. "Abort" any time. LEAVING THE TEST AREA = alert + the test STOPPED (nothing is sent to the boat, no mode change).

passages.heading: THE PRACTICAL TEST ON THE BOAT (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test on THIS boat")
passages.text: 4. Every task approved -> "Final approval": the boat asks for CONFIRM on the ONBOARD joystick within 10 s (a confirm-only question that changes NOTHING on the boat; stick centred, like every CONFIRM). Confirmed -> the level goes up (logged with the examiner, the ride file and the question number). Then send the academy levels file to the gateway (next login). The confirm-only question is refused while another CONFIRM request waits (power raise, AUTO ...), in UNCREWED and in FIRST TEST; STANDBY cancels it.

passages.heading: THE TEST AREA (ground station: menu Academy -> "Practical test area")
passages.text: The area in git is a PLACEHOLDER (not surveyed): the practical test refuses it. An instructor (a valid CAPTAIN with 2FA) sets the real one on site: "Add point (boat GPS)" at each corner, the ramp top / bottom from the boat GPS, or taps on the drawing, or "Import .geojson". "Save area" writes academy/data/test_area.json (logged). It is NEVER a chart: no safety check uses it.

passages.heading: CAPTAIN AND COPILOT (the gateway decides, every station shows it)
passages.text: CAPTAIN holds the manual licence and sits at screen 1 (cameras + joystick). Holds HELM. The ONLY one who can start REMOTE MANUAL or MANEUVER. The captain's own actions go straight to the boat.

passages.heading: CAPTAIN AND COPILOT (the gateway decides, every station shows it)
passages.text: COPILOT everything except manual driving: routes, AUTO, HEADING LOCK adjustments, maximum speed, AIS / collision, status - also while the captain drives. Every copilot action that changes the driving appears on the CAPTAIN'S SCREEN 1 as a question: ACCEPT -> sent, REJECT / 10 s / screen 1 closed -> refused. STANDBY, HOLD (AUTO pause) and AUTO RETURN never wait (the return still needs the joystick CONFIRM on the boat; in REMOTE / MANEUVER the return waits for the ACCEPT too and the boat refuses it there). The copilot can't take HELM (code 117) or ask for manual driving (code 118).

passages.heading: CAPTAIN AND COPILOT (the gateway decides, every station shows it)
passages.text: The first licensed user who logs in is the captain; everybody else is a copilot (a viewer only watches). A station on the boat can always take HELM and then is the captain. ROLE SWAP: either side asks, the other one accepts - only if BOTH hold the licence. HELM moves to the new captain in one step, so an UNCREWED boat never sees a lost link. SINGLE-OPERATOR mode (one person, both screens): your own confirmation instead of the captain's ACCEPT; manual driving still needs the licence.

passages.heading: GENERATOR MODE (the engine charges the 12 V bank at a fast idle in NEUTRAL)
passages.text: This is the ONE thing on the boat that opens the throttle by itself - and only in NEUTRAL, only while every condition below holds (checked every step, app/generator.c): * "GENERATOR AUTO ON" was pressed by the captain (screen 2, control panel; a copilot's press is a question on the captain's screen 1). It is OFF after every power-up; the STANDBY button switches it OFF again (until somebody switches it on).

passages.heading: GENERATOR MODE (the engine charges the 12 V bank at a fast idle in NEUTRAL)
passages.text: * the boat is in STANDBY (not stopping), the outputs are armed, the gear is NEUTRAL and the NEUTRAL SWITCH confirms it (a boat without the switch never runs the generator), no engine kill, no e-stop, no safety-monitor trip, not FIRST TEST, no alarm that is not an advisory (acknowledge first - LOW BATTERY is an advisory and does not block it), the bank voltage is measured and below gen_start_v 12.1 V.

passages.heading: GENERATOR MODE (the engine charges the 12 V bank at a fast idle in NEUTRAL)
passages.text: What it does: beep + notice GENERATOR STARTING, 10 s later the fast idle (gen_idle_pct 8 %), then +2 % every 30 s while the voltage (fast filter) still falls, hold when it stops falling (that throttle is remembered in the data flash and is the first step next time), -2 % every 30 s when the bank rises above 12.5 V. Never above min(gen_max_pct 25 %, 30 %, the power limit). Cycle: 20 min, then 1 min at idle and a rest-voltage check: still low -> again; recovered -> GENERATOR DONE (notice, auto stays on).

passages.heading: GENERATOR MODE (the engine charges the 12 V bank at a fast idle in NEUTRAL)
passages.text: Every stop is idle FIRST (the throttle comes down at its normal rate and nothing opens it again until it is idle): the captain's OFF, the STANDBY button, a joystick deflection, any alarm, any mode / gear request (also a pending AUTO start waiting for CONFIRM), link lost (UNCREWED), e-stop, engine kill, no voltage data. GEAR FAULT: the neutral switch opens while it runs, or the boat speeds up (SOG + 0.5 kn within 20 s of a throttle rise) -> throttle idle at once (the fast STANDBY closing rate), alarm GEAR, generator auto OFF until it is switched on again (acknowledge the alarm first).

passages.heading: GENERATOR MODE (the engine charges the 12 V bank at a fast idle in NEUTRAL)
passages.text: CPU1 watches it too: throttle above idle in neutral is allowed only while core 0 says "generator active" and at most the generator cap; the gear leaving neutral meanwhile = trip (safe outputs, latched). Screens: screen 2 status panel row "Generator" + the button; screen 1 bottom line "GEN x %" while it runs; notices STARTING / FAULT / DONE. Parameters (Config tab, STANDBY only): gen_max_pct 0..30 (0 = generator disabled; set from the boat file's generator_max_pct when the HELM station connects, chapter 5), gen_start_v 11.5..13 V, gen_idle_pct 3..15 %. Log: event 24 GENERATOR (every state change and throttle step), TELEM2 group L.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: The relays of the boat file (chapter 5) are switched by an 8-16 channel Modbus RTU relay board on an RS485 line from the AURIX (hal/tc_modbus.c, app/relays.c; board, pins and baud rate TBD: WIRING.md 3D). NO relay is in any control path: a relay never changes the mode, the throttle, the gear, the steering or a thruster.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * The relay TABLE (which channel is what) comes from the boat file: the HELM station sends it when it connects in STANDBY. The AURIX keeps it in its data flash. The same table as the stored one = taken at once. A DIFFERENT table is taken only in STANDBY and only after the joystick CONFIRM within 10 s (the banner "CONFIRM: RELAY TABLE"; CREWED: the onboard joystick, UNCREWED: the shore joystick) - until then the stored table stays in use (a wrong boat file must not move the STARTER out of the engine rules). No CONFIRM = the station offers it again later.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: While ANY other CONFIRM is waiting (a power raise, AUTO start ...) the table is not offered (the AURIX refuses it then): yours goes first. In single-operator mode the station asks you first ("send the relay table?") - it never confirms by itself. Without any table no relay can be switched. A relay channel must exist on the fitted board (8-16 channels): a table with a higher channel is refused.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * onoff / latching: on / off. momentary: a pulse timed BY THE BOARD (at most max_s, never more than 5 s - it ends even if the AURIX stops). timed: on, and switched off by the AURIX after max_s. If a momentary relay is still on 0.5 s after its pulse should have ended (the board's timer failed), the AURIX switches it OFF itself and keeps trying until the readback shows it off. An interlocked pair (TRIM UP / TRIM DOWN): never both - the second request is refused while the other one is on.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * Engine relays follow their ROLE (never the type or the name): the STARTER is never pulsed by a plain relay command - only the START button of the engine page (ENGINE CONTROLS below). IGNITION switches ON only with the engine conditions (throttle idle, gear neutral confirmed, e-stop released, no ENGINE KILL / monitor trip latched); SHUTOFF ON (= stop the engine) is ALWAYS allowed (also while driving, with the e-stop pressed or the kill latched: stopping is never refused); OFF always.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: A SHUTOFF ON the relay board can't take yet (silent, or not seen yet in the first second after a reset) is kept and sent as soon as the board answers - for 10 s, then it is dropped (check the engine: press SHUTOFF again).

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * power_up "on" is applied only ONCE, only with the first table after the AURIX's own power-on (never after a watchdog / software reset or a reconnect: then the board's states are read back and kept), and it only switches ON. Nothing is ever switched OFF by itself; engine relays are never switched automatically.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * The board is read back every 100 ms. No valid reply for 3 s -> RELAY BOARD SILENT (an advisory: states shown unknown, no new relay command, no buzzer, nothing else changes). It clears by itself when the board answers again; an OFF that was waiting is then carried out. With no board fitted at all (HAL_RELAY_FITTED 0) there is no such alarm.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * FIRST TEST: no relay changes at all. A monitor trip / the e-stop leave the relays as they are (the board is not a safety path). * THE RELAY BOARD ON DRONECAN (step 11f - a BUILD OPTION, hal_pins.h RELAY_BUS; the default stays the RS485 board until the board is chosen): the relay board can also be the DroneCAN node 30 on the servo bus (relays 1-6 = hardpoints 0-5). Every rule above stays exactly the same (the AURIX's relay code does not know the bus). What is different:

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: - the AURIX sends a new state 10 times at 50 Hz, then nothing (the board holds it); after ANY reset of the AURIX it sends nothing until you switch a relay - a reset never switches anything. - momentary relays (TRIM, the STARTER) are timed by the AURIX: ON frames at 50 Hz while the pulse / START hold lasts. If the AURIX stops (frozen, reset, cable) the board's own command timeout (<= 300 ms) switches the relay off. The STARTER is always also behind the hardware time-limit relay (about 6 s: WIRING.md 3D / 3E).

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: - readback = the board's hardpoint.Status, if the board sends it. A board that does not: the relays panel says "no readback from the relay board: the COMMANDED states are shown"; after an AURIX power-on while the board kept running the states are unknown until you switch them (a relay paired with an unknown, not momentary partner is refused until the partner was switched once - switch it OFF first).

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: - RELAY BOARD SILENT also when node 30 is not OPERATIONAL, reports ERROR, or the CAN bus is down; health WARNING = a notice only. A board that loses power or reboots has every relay OFF afterwards; the AURIX never switches them back on by itself.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: - a relay switched ON just as the board drops off the bus (step 13h): the AURIX never switches it OFF by itself. If the board is back within 10 s of your command, has NOT rebooted, and you did not change that relay meanwhile, the ON is completed; otherwise nothing is sent, the relay shows unknown (OFF after a board reboot) and you press again. The STARTER and other press-and-hold relays are never completed late.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: RELAY BUTTONS (the stations; requests only - the AURIX decides every time) * Screen 2: the panel "RELAYS" (collapsible; the station puts it in the corner with the most room, never over the boat) shows the boat file's relays by group: ENGINE (IGNITION, START (hold), SHUTOFF + RESTART), TRIM, EXTRA. An interlocked pair (TRIM UP / TRIM DOWN) is on one line. Lit = on, grey = state unknown (board silent, table not active yet): a grey button does nothing. onoff / latching / timed: a click switches it on / off. momentary "(hold)": press and HOLD - the relay runs while you hold it (a board-timed pulse of at most max_s) and goes off when you let go.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: START (hold) = the engine page's START. While the table is not yet active on the boat (or waits for the CONFIRM) the panel says so and the buttons are grey.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * Screen 1: the relays with "show_hud": true in a small box left of the picture (hidden in MINIMAL). Trim / extra relays are buttons (momentary = press and hold); engine relays are only shown there (lamp) - switch them on screen 2.

passages.heading: RELAY BOARD (RS485 Modbus RTU: lights, pumps, trim, engine switches)
passages.text: * Only the HELM station's relay commands are carried out (the AURIX checks it). A copilot's ENGINE relay (IGNITION / SHUTOFF) waits for the captain's ACCEPT on screen 1; a copilot's TRIM / EXTRA relay goes straight. The gateway knows the groups from the relay table the station sent (kept on its SSD, state/relay_tables.json); a table it doesn't know = every relay waits for the captain's ACCEPT (the station then sends the same table once more so the gateway learns it). Log: event 25 RELAY (commands, table events, readback changes, board lost / back); TELEM2 group M.

passages.heading: ENGINE CONTROLS + REMOTE RESTART (Tools -> Engine)
passages.text: The engine page of the HELM station: the boat file's engine switches (IGNITION, SHUTOFF: ON / OFF), START (hold) and RESTART. Order: IGNITION on -> hold START -> SHUTOFF to stop. The engine kill stays its own AURIX output, never a relay.

passages.heading: ENGINE CONTROLS + REMOTE RESTART (Tools -> Engine)
passages.text: * IGNITION ON: the same conditions as below (idle, neutral, e-stop released) - refused while you drive. SHUTOFF ON (stop the engine): always, no conditions. * Every time, on the boat: you hold HELM, the throttle output is idle, the gear is in neutral (the neutral switch if fitted, else the gear servo at N), the e-stop is released, not the FIRST TEST build. Otherwise refused with the reason (shown on the page). NO code, NO joystick CONFIRM, NO waiting time, NO limit on the attempts.

passages.heading: ENGINE CONTROLS + REMOTE RESTART (Tools -> Engine)
passages.text: * START (hold): while you hold the button the station sends START 5 times a second; each one keeps a 300 ms STARTER pulse on the relay board (timed by the board itself). At most 5 s per hold, then 10 s cool-down (also after a shorter hold; never past 5 s: with less than 0.1 s of the hold left the hold simply ends). The starter stops at once when you let go (or no START for 0.3 s), the link / HELM is lost, the e-stop is pressed, the gear leaves neutral (also a joystick takeover), the throttle opens, or the STANDBY button is pressed. There is no tacho yet: time limit only.

passages.heading: ENGINE CONTROLS + REMOTE RESTART (Tools -> Engine)
passages.text: * RESTART after an ENGINE KILL (lost link, UNCREWED): clears the kill. The boat stays in STANDBY at idle / neutral - nothing starts by itself; then START the engine. The next lost link kills it again. * RESTART after a SAFETY MONITOR trip: the monitor's latch can only go with a reset, so the AURIX restarts itself (a software reset, log event 27 RESTART written first, about 0.5 s later). Everything starts again as after power-on: neutral-start interlock, power limit 30 / 5 %, boot counter + 1; the relay board keeps its relays (no power_up states). If the conditions fail before the reset (e.g. the e-stop is pressed), the reset is cancelled.

passages.heading: ENGINE CONTROLS + REMOTE RESTART (Tools -> Engine)
passages.text: * A copilot's RESTART waits for the captain's ACCEPT on screen 1; START is the captain's only (gateway code 118). CREWED: the person on board can always use the key as well. Log: event 27 RESTART (kill cleared / reset / START begins / stops / refused, with the reason); TELEM2 group O.

passages.heading: DP THRUSTERS (the thrusters themselves; the DP mode is the next part)
passages.text: Dynamic positioning (Minn Kota style) uses two small electric thrusters on the 12 V bank: a bow TUNNEL thruster (sideways) and a fixed transom motor (fore / aft). This part drives and protects them; only the DP mode below ever asks them for thrust - outside DP they ALWAYS stay at 0.

passages.heading: DP THRUSTERS (the thrusters themselves; the DP mode is the next part)
passages.text: * The boat file's "thrusters" block (chapter 5) reaches the boat when the HELM station holds HELM in STANDBY (RAM only, again after every boat restart; TELEM2 group N shows what the boat took). No settings = no thruster fitted = never any thrust.

passages.heading: DP THRUSTERS (the thrusters themselves; the DP mode is the next part)
passages.text: * Only one part of the software writes them (app/thruster.c): never more than the file's max_pct, changes at most 50 %/s, 0 at once on every stop, and 0 whenever DP is not active. * Heat budget per thruster: running fills it (1 s per s), standing still empties it (run_s / rest_s per s). Used up (run_s of running) = that thruster stops until it has rested (rest_s), alarm DP THRUSTER HOT; the other thruster runs on.

passages.heading: DP THRUSTERS (the thrusters themselves; the DP mode is the next part)
passages.text: * The safety monitor (CPU1) knows when DP is active and the caps: thrust without DP, or above a cap, trips it, and its safe state puts both thrusters to 0 (also with core 0 frozen). The e-stop cuts the thruster power with its own contactor and the software sends 0 within one step. * Never in the FIRST TEST build, never before the outputs are armed, never on the big boat. Hardware: WIRING.md 3C (TBD: thrusters, controllers, pins, contactor). Log: event 28 DP (settings taken, thruster HOT, cooled down).

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: While DP runs the OUTBOARD stays at idle in NEUTRAL with its steering held the whole time (only the generator may open its throttle in neutral, see GENERATOR MODE); the two thrusters do everything. * SPOT (Spot-Lock): the boat holds the GPS position where DP started and the heading it had (the anchor heading). +1 / -1 / +10 / -10 (the panel course buttons, or the station's heading buttons) turn the held heading.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * JOG: moves the spot 1.5 m (boat file jog_m) ahead / astern / to port / to starboard of the held heading; back to SPOT once there. * CRUISE: holds a heading and a speed over ground on the stern motor (0 .. 3 kn, dp_max_kn TO CONFIRM); speed and heading can be changed.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * TRIP: drives the stored AUTO program at a set speed (at most 3 kn; the legs' own speeds still apply); the gateway's speed cap / avoidance heading work as in AUTO (also the lost lease: hold the heading, slow, DRIVER DECISION); at the last waypoint (or a STOP waypoint) it switches to SPOT there. A new program can't be uploaded while a TRIP runs.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * Start: the HELM station asks (PROTO_T_DP; a copilot's request needs the captain's ACCEPT) and the joystick CONFIRM follows within 10 s (CREWED: the onboard joystick; UNCREWED: the shore captain's joystick). Only from STANDBY (not stopping) - or straight from REMOTE MANUAL / MANEUVER (owner 2026-10-31) - outputs armed, GPS trusted, compass working, slower than 2 kn, both thrusters set up by the boat file and not hot, the outboard at idle (the modelled throttle servo position) and in neutral - only a running generator may carry its neutral throttle into SPOT. Never in the FIRST TEST build. In DP: SPOT starts at once (it only holds the boat where it is); CRUISE / TRIP need the CONFIRM again.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * The end - the thrusters go to 0 FIRST, then STANDBY: DP STOP (a copilot may always send it, without the captain's ACCEPT), the STANDBY button, the e-stop, any fault (gear, joystick, monitor ...), UNCREWED link lost, GPS lost or suspect (no dead reckoning in DP), the compass lost for 10 s (the gyro holds the heading meanwhile; no gyro: at once), a thruster HOT (it can't hold with one), pushed more than 50 m off the spot or off it for 2 min (TO CONFIRM).

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: The onboard joystick (CREWED) ALWAYS wins: deflect it / TAKE = thrusters 0 at once and MANUAL on the outboard (alarm JOYSTICK, like every takeover). * Advisories (DP keeps trying, the power limit stays): DP OFF SPOT (pushed farther than spot_alarm_m, 15 m, off the spot), DP OVERPOWER (both thrusters at their limit for 10 s).

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * Limits of a bow tunnel thruster: it pushes the bow sideways AND turns the boat, so it can't move the boat sideways while it holds the heading. The heading comes first: in a current or wind from the SIDE the boat slowly drifts off the spot (DP OFF SPOT). Turn the bow into the current (+1 / +10) - then the stern motor holds it.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * Generator in DP: it may run while DP holds (SPOT / JOG); a CRUISE / TRIP start stops it (idle first). If the stern motor has to push astern hard (> 30 % for 5 s) while the boat is still pushed ahead off the spot, the gearbox may not be in neutral: GEAR FAULT, the generator idles, auto off, DP ends.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: TELEM2 group N (sub-state, spot error ahead / to starboard, held heading, speeds, waypoint, why it ended); log event 28 DP (start / sub-state, JOG, TRIP end, stop + why). On the ground station (step 11): * Screen 2, the bottom-left control panel: with both thrusters set up (the boat file's thruster settings taken) a line "DP:" with SPOT / CRUISE / TRIP and the speed for CRUISE / TRIP (- / +, 0.5 .. 3 kn). While a start waits for the joystick CONFIRM the panel says so; DP STOP cancels it.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: In DP the mode buttons and the AUTO rows are replaced by: the DP state (sub-state + distance from the spot), DP STOP, the generator button; SPOT / CRUISE / TRIP (+ "TRIP: continue" after a STOP waypoint) and the speed (SET sends a new CRUISE / TRIP speed); in SPOT / JOG the JOG arrows (up = ahead, down = astern, left = port, right = starboard; one step = jog_m) and where the spot is ("spot 2.0 m ahead, 1.5 m to port", red when DP OFF SPOT). The panel's +1 / -1 / +10 / -10 turn the DP heading. The status panel shows the DP line (sub-state and the main number) and the held heading.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: A copilot's SPOT / CRUISE / TRIP / JOG / speed waits for the captain's ACCEPT; DP STOP never waits.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * Screen 1: the DP box in the CDI place (bottom middle, like MANEUVER): the title (sub-state, distance from the spot), the spot vector (the boat in the middle with its bow up; the dot = the spot: up = ahead, right = starboard; the square's edge = spot_alarm_m) and the thrust bars B (bow, sideways) and S (stern, fore / aft) from the middle, -100 .. +100 %; amber when a thruster is hot or the boat is off the spot. Display only.

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: * The gateway checks a TRIP start like an AUTO start: across or near shallow water refused (code 114), out of the geofence refused (120) (also "continue": from the DP's next waypoint; the leg from the boat to the first waypoint and the geofence as it is NOW are checked). A program the gateway has not checked itself - loaded over the USB cable, from the boat's memory after a power-up, or before a gateway restart - can't start a TRIP (code 121 "route not checked by the gateway"): send the route again from screen 2 ("Send route").

passages.heading: DP MODE (SPOT / JOG / CRUISE / TRIP) - the thrusters hold or move the boat
passages.text: In a TRIP the collision avoidance works as in AUTO (slow down, route astern, DRIVER DECISION; the slowest speed asked in DP is 1 kn); in SPOT / JOG / CRUISE a collision danger is the COLLISION RISK + DRIVER DECISION alarm only - nothing is steered or slowed, the driver decides (DP STOP, the joystick). * Speed on the screens in DP: the boat's dead reckoning takes its speed from the outboard (idle in DP), so in DP with the GPS trusted the screens and the gateway use the GPS speed / course.

passages.heading: WHAT IT IS
passages.text: The T.16000M stick steers (left / right = outboard angle). The TWCS throttle has a lever that STAYS where you leave it (it has no spring), with a NEUTRAL ZONE in the middle (45-55 % of its travel): above the neutral zone = forward (further = more throttle) inside the neutral zone = idle + neutral below the neutral zone = reverse

passages.heading: WHAT IT IS
passages.text: Gear changes always go idle -> neutral -> gear, however fast you move it. Both plug into a small powered USB hub, the hub into the Teensy bridge, the bridge into the AURIX (WIRING.md section 6). If anything in that chain fails - a plug, the hub, the Teensy, the wire - the boat sees JOYSTICK FAULT within 0.15-0.2 s, exactly like a broken wire on the analog stick: if the joystick was driving: throttle idle + neutral, STANDBY, alarm; the gyro holds the course until idle + neutral, then the steering stops. The T.16000M and the TWCS are NOT waterproof: dry console only.

passages.heading: SWITCH THE BOAT TO THE USB JOYSTICK (once)
passages.text: 1. Ground station, Joystick tab: Source = "USB bridge", Throttle = "lever". 2. "Factory default (T.16000M + TWCS)" fills in the default buttons. 3. Boat in STANDBY -> SAVE TO BOAT. It is stored with a checksum and used at every power-up. (Back to the wired joystick the same way.)

passages.heading: DEFAULT BUTTONS (change them with "Map buttons", below)
passages.text: TAKE stick trigger (stick button 1) STANDBY stick thumb button (stick button 2) AUTO TWCS button 1 CONFIRM TWCS button 4 (clearly apart from AUTO) HDG LOCK TWCS button 3 -1 / +1 TWCS hat left / right -10 / +10 TWCS hat down / up SAVE stick button 3 (video SAVE on the gateway; optional) Which physical button is "TWCS button 1/3/4" depends on the TWCS: check with learn mode or the "now" column of the Joystick tab and map them where your thumb finds them. The panel STANDBY button stays and always wins.

passages.heading: POWER-UP
passages.text: The lever must be IN THE NEUTRAL ZONE and the stick centred. Otherwise: alarm "JOYSTICK NOT CENTRED" (= not in neutral), the joystick is ignored and the outputs stay off. Put the lever in neutral, let go of the stick.

passages.heading: TAKING OVER (any mode)
passages.text: * stick sideways (past 15 % for 0.1 s), or * the TAKE button, or * moving the lever more than 10 % away from where it was at the last hand-back (it was in neutral then, so: leaving the neutral zone). In HDG LOCK the lever IS the throttle, so there it does not take over.

passages.heading: THROTTLE PICKUP (no surprise jump)
passages.text: When the lever gets the throttle (MANUAL or HDG LOCK entered from STANDBY, AUTO or TRAINING), it first does NOTHING. The yellow banner says "MOVE THROTTLE TO PICK UP: lever to xx %" and the lever bar shows a yellow mark. Move the lever to that mark (within 3 %), or through it, or into the neutral zone: from then on the lever drives, starting from the throttle the engine has now.

passages.heading: THROTTLE PICKUP (no surprise jump)
passages.text: * Coming from AUTO: the engine keeps its throttle (lowered to the 30 % power limit that every takeover sets) until you pick it up. * Coming from STANDBY: the engine stays at idle + neutral; the pickup point is the neutral zone. Example: the lever was left at 80 % and you take over: nothing happens until you bring the lever to the mark (or neutral).

passages.heading: LEVER AND POWER LIMIT
passages.text: Full lever forward = the CURRENT power limit (30 % at start), full lever back = the reverse limit (5 % at start). Raising the limit never makes the boat speed up by itself: if the lever is fully forward when you raise from 30 to 50 %, the throttle stays at 30 %. Pull the lever back a little and push it forward again - now full lever is 50 %.

passages.heading: HAND-BACK
passages.text: Stick centred AND lever in the neutral zone, then AUTO (or panel HDG LOCK). Otherwise refused + chirp. (This means the engine is at idle when you hand back.)

passages.heading: CONFIRM (power raise, AUTO start / resume) on the USB button follows the
passages.text: same rules as before: only with the stick centred and the joystick armed, only for a pending PC request. The lever position does not matter here.

passages.heading: MAP BUTTONS (ground station, Joystick tab, boat in STANDBY)
passages.text: 1. "Map buttons (guided)". Let go of everything, click Next. 2. Move the stick fully right, hold, Next (steering axis found). 3. Push the lever fully forward, hold, Next (throttle axis + direction). 4. For each function press the button you want. A button already used for another function is refused at once ("already TAKE - press a different button"). TAKE, AUTO and CONFIRM must be mapped; the others can be skipped.

passages.heading: MAP BUTTONS (ground station, Joystick tab, boat in STANDBY)
passages.text: 5. SAVE TO BOAT. The boat checks again: TAKE, AUTO and CONFIRM on the same button -> refused ("two functions share a button"). Note: the buttons keep their OLD job while you map them - pressing the TAKE button switches to MANUAL. That is on purpose (the joystick is never switched off). Press the panel STANDBY before saving. One function only: the "Map" button in its row.

passages.heading: LEARN MODE (on the Teensy, to see what is what)
passages.text: Teensy on the PC USB, VS Code -> PlatformIO -> Monitor, type l + Enter. Every button / hat / axis you move is printed with its code number. While learn mode is on the boat keeps the USB joystick disarmed. Other joysticks than the Thrustmaster: calibrate first ( c ), see bridge/README.md.

passages.heading: STATUS TO WATCH (Joystick strip / tab)
passages.text: "USB bridge: 100 frames/s, CRC errors 0, stick OK, throttle OK" is normal. Fewer frames/s, growing CRC errors: bad wire / interference. More than 5 CRC errors per second, a frozen counter, an unplugged device, an invalid axis or no frame for 0.15 s = JOYSTICK FAULT (the reason is shown). For the first 5 s after power-up the bridge may still be starting (USB): no alarm then, the joystick is just not armed yet.

passages.heading: MEASURED IN THE SIMULATION (bridge + hub modelled)
passages.text: TAKE pressed -> mode change on the AURIX: average 34 ms, worst 60 ms (200 presses; target < 100 ms). Worst case by design: USB + hub 2 ms + frame period 10 ms + UART 3 ms + control loop 50 ms = 65 ms.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The gateway PC on the boat (a Lenovo ThinkPad L390 Yoga with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Windows 11) is the only way in from the internet. The AURIX is NEVER on the network: it talks only to the gateway PC, over a cable (UART, the same frames with checksum as the USB laptop link). The gateway PC sits on the boat LAN behind the Teltonika router; shore PCs and the iPhone reach it only through a VPN (Tailscale) that the boat opens itself - no open ports, works behind the 4G operator's CGNAT. The USB laptop, the onboard joystick and the STANDBY button work exactly as before, with or without the gateway PC. Setup step by step: gateway\README.md.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: QUICK SETUP (Ubuntu 24.04, one command, gateway\README.md section 0): on the gateway PC, after installing Ubuntu, run curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alextrygons/trygons-c2/main/gateway/setup_all.sh | sudo bash

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: (or, from a clone: sudo bash ~/trygons-c2/gateway/setup_all.sh). It asks only: the boat name, the gateway users and their passwords (not shown; stored as hashes in /etc/trygons/secrets.json, never in git or in the log), the Tailscale key (not shown), which Ethernet port goes to the router and which to the cameras (unplug / plug in the cable when it says so), the chart area and which USB adapter is the AURIX / the AIS receiver (an adapter that isn't plugged in stays "TBD": plug it in and run it again).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The AURIX adapter must be confirmed as a 3.3 V TTL USB-UART adapter (answer "no" = refused, TBD); one the list flags as probably RS232 is refused unless you answer an explicit yes (Enter = no). Then it installs and checks everything by itself and ends with a check list of OK / FAIL lines (service steady, AURIX link in the log of THIS run, MediaMTX, vision Python + model, charts, apt ...). "ALL OK" only when every line is OK AND no step failed. The upgrade never restarts services by itself (NEEDRESTART_MODE=l): the final reboot does. Tailscale name of the gateway PC: trygons-gw-<boat> (e.g. trygons-gw-rf49d).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The firewall (nftables.conf) is NOT applied by the script (gateway\README.md section 8): the check list says so in a WARN line (not counted in ALL OK). Re-running it rewrites the gateway's service, lid and battery files and the UTC time zone (edit them in the repository, not on the PC). Safe to run again (Enter keeps what is there). --dry-run shows what it would do without changing anything; --lang en = English (Greek is the default); --checks = only the check list (after the reboot it asks for: all OK). It never opens the AURIX UART. Run it in harbour, the boat in STANDBY.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The gateway PC: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is recommended at sea (no forced updates or restarts); Windows 11 works too (Windows Update set to "ask, never restart"). It starts by itself at boot and restarts after a crash (Ubuntu: a systemd service; Windows: the Task Scheduler task "Trygons Gateway"). Power: a 12 V -> USB-C PD car charger from the bank; its own battery is the UPS (charge limit 80 %: TLP / Lenovo Vantage); it keeps running with the lid closed. Ethernet to the router and to the camera PoE switch (USB-Ethernet adapters if it has no RJ45). The AIS receiver is a USB one. The serial devices are named in gateway.json by a stable id (python gateway.py --list-serial).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: A. THE GATEWAY LINK (AURIX <-> gateway PC) * UART 921600 baud (AURIX ASCLIN1: P15.0 -> adapter RXD, P15.1 <- adapter TXD) through a 3.3 V TTL USB-UART adapter (FTDI / CP2102 at 3.3 V) on the gateway PC. NEVER an RS232 port or cable: its +-12 V destroys the AURIX pins (WIRING.md section 7).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * The AURIX sends the gateway PC: telemetry, and a COMPLETE COPY of its log (every record it writes to its SD card, numbered). The gateway PC writes it to its SSD as .TLG files (aurix_logs\YYYYMMDD\P<boot>_<file>.TLG) - readable with logview.py / log2csv.py like the SD card files.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * If the cable is too slow at some moment, the AURIX drops records for the gateway PC FIRST - never control traffic. The gateway PC notes the missing numbers in gaps.csv. The AURIX SD card is always complete: it stays the independent black box.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * The gateway PC sends a status once a second (its "I'm alive"). Silent for 3 s: alarm GATEWAY LOST. Nothing else changes (no mode change) - unless you are driving remotely (part D). * The gateway PC's SSD missing / failing: alarm GATEWAY STORAGE; everything else keeps running. The data are on the gateway PC's own SSD.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * TIME: the AURIX sends GPS time to the gateway PC once a second; the gateway PC sets its clock from it, so the boat log, the gateway logs and the video all have the same time. * Ground station, System tab: "gateway: OK / LOST, gateway log copy up to record N, gaps".

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: B. USERS, ROLES AND HELM * Every station logs in to the gateway (user + password, or a key). VIEWER = watch only. HELM = may hold HELM. * Only ONE station holds HELM; only its commands are carried out (the AURIX checks it; others get "NOT HELM"). The top bar of the ground station shows "HELM: YOU - ..." or who has it; buttons "Take HELM" / "Release".

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * A station ON THE BOAT (USB laptop, boat LAN) can always take HELM, also from a remote one. A remote station only when nobody has it. The USB laptop takes a free HELM by itself. * The onboard joystick and the STANDBY button still beat everything. Power raise, AUTO start / resume and remote driving still need the joystick CONFIRM on the boat - remote can never do them alone.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * Every command carries station, number and time; the gateway refuses duplicates, old ones (more than 2 s), out-of-order and too many. A PC with a wrong clock is fine (the gateway measures the difference). * Slow or far links get reduced telemetry (2 times a second, the essentials) automatically; the System tab shows every station's latency.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * Remote HELM station lost: alarm REMOTE LINK LOST, HELM back to nobody, no mode change (remote driving: part D). * TRUST: which station is "on the boat" is decided by the gateway PC (where it connects from); the AURIX can't check it. A faulty or hacked gateway PC could therefore claim to be a station on the boat. What it still can't do: leave MANUAL against the joystick, override STANDBY, start AUTO / remote driving or raise the power without the joystick CONFIRM on board, steer outside AUTO, or go faster than the power limit.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * iPhone: http://trygons-gw:8080 over the VPN, view only (HELM from the web page only if switched on in the gateway config). * Audit log on the gateway PC: who connected, who held HELM, every command and its answer. Security rules: gateway\README.md section 12 - please do all of them (change ALL default passwords, VPN only, cameras without internet, separate networks).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * Connect the ground station through the gateway: python app.py gw:trygons-gw:5761 (asks for user + password) C. INTERNET CHANNELS (router Teltonika RUT901) Channels: 4G (SIM 1), 4G SIM 2, RF (future), STARLINK. STARLINK = EMERGENCY ONLY: metered, never used for sync, and in AUTO only when every other channel is down. The RUT901 has two SIM slots but one modem: only one SIM works at a time (switching takes 30-90 s; SIM 2 shows "standby").

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Ground station, Network tab: every channel with up/down, internet, latency, loss, signal (4G), data used today / this month; the active one marked ">". Buttons:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: AUTO failover by priority (4G, 4G SIM 2, RF); STARLINK only when all are down; back to a normal channel when it has been stable for 60 s.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: MANUAL <ch> use this channel; if it has no internet for 30 s -> the next working one + alarm CHANNEL FALLBACK; back when it is stable again. STARLINK asks "EMERGENCY LINK - metered data" first. The fallback is STARLINK only if no normal channel works (your chosen one included).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: MANUAL STRICT only this channel, never switch. Only from a station on the boat, with a warning.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: KEEP every switch you ask for is a TRIAL: press KEEP within 60 s (over the new link). If you can't (the new link is dead), the gateway goes back to what worked - you can never lock yourself out from shore. It goes back to STARLINK only if you had chosen STARLINK yourself; otherwise it picks again (a normal channel first).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Only the HELM station or a station on the boat may change the channel. While STARLINK is active: big "STARLINK - EMERGENCY LINK" banner, data saver ON (reduced telemetry, cameras front only, low - part E), sync stopped (part G), data counter for this session and the month, warning at the monthly limit you set (gateway.json, monthly_warn_gb, 20 GB).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Setup of the RUT901 and Starlink: gateway\README.md section 13 (LAN range 10.42.0.x FIRST, then Starlink in bypass mode on the WAN port, failover with health checks, SSH key for the gateway PC). D. REMOTE JOYSTICK DRIVING FROM A SHORE PC (mode REMOTE MANUAL) RULE: somebody is ALWAYS on board while the boat is driven remotely. Priority, always: STANDBY button > onboard joystick > remote joystick > autopilot modes.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: On the shore PC: plug in a USB joystick (e.g. T.16000M + TWCS; any standard joystick works). Ground station connected through the gateway (gw:...), Remote tab: 1. "Find joysticks" shows the devices with their numbers. Choose the device + axis for steering and for the throttle, "invert" if it goes the wrong way, "lever" for the TWCS. Save.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 2. Take HELM. Tick "send my joystick (30 Hz)". 3. REMOTE MANUAL on screen 1. CREWED: the boat shows "PRESS JOYSTICK CONFIRM - REMOTE DRIVING": the person ON BOARD presses CONFIRM within 10 s. UNCREWED (owner 2026-10-31): no CONFIRM - it starts at once, only with your stick centred and the lever at neutral (else "centre the joystick" and nothing starts). The mode becomes REMOTE MANUAL (blue).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 4. Drive: stick X = outboard angle (rate-limited, 20 deg/s), lever = throttle with the neutral zone and THROTTLE PICKUP like on board (chapter 8). Maximum 20 % forward / 5 % reverse (and never above the power limit). Slamming reduction applies (part H).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 5. When done: choose another mode - STANDBY (idle, neutral, steering off), AUTO or DP (their start rules), or MANEUVER. There is NO RELEASE (not on the screen, not on the joystick): a release by accident in the middle of a manoeuvre would be dangerous.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: STANDBY button while driving remotely: the shore stick is ignored at once; the gyro holds the course until idle + neutral, then the steering is held. It also ends when: the onboard joystick moves or TAKE is pressed (-> MANUAL at once), STANDBY is pressed, any fault, a station on board takes HELM, the remote driver's link fails.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: LINK PROBLEMS: joystick data older than 0.3 s, a gap of 0.3 s, or a link latency over 0.4 s -> at once: throttle to idle, neutral, the outboard holds the heading on the gyro, alarm REMOTE DRIVING LINK LOST. After 5 s without the link: STANDBY. It NEVER starts again by itself - a new REMOTE MANUAL (CREWED: + CONFIRM on board) is needed. The joystick packets travel by UDP (signed with a key the gateway gives at login): a lost packet is simply replaced by the next one 33 ms later.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: (By TCP, one lost packet would hold everything for 0.2-0.6 s and the boat would declare LINK LOST every few seconds on 4G.) Measured in the simulation (4G, ~80 ms round trip, 1 % packet loss): stick move on shore -> visible in the boat's telemetry: median ~185 ms, max ~230 ms; 60 s of driving without a single LINK LOST.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: E. CAMERAS (4 x TP-Link Tapo C310) FRONT-1 (main), FRONT-2 (backup), REAR-LEFT, REAR-RIGHT. Cable (Ethernet), on their own camera network behind the gateway PC; they have NO internet (the cloud is not used). The gateway PC relays the video (MediaMTX, no re-encoding). Video is never needed for safety: a camera problem never changes the mode.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Ground station, Cameras tab (the big driver screen comes in part I):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Full front HIGH, mirrors LOW

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Front only front LOW, mirrors off

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Mirrors only rear cameras LOW

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: All off no video (no data used)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Only what you asked for is sent over the internet. On STARLINK (or with data saver) only the front camera LOW is allowed - "override" works with data saver on 4G, never on STARLINK. Per camera: state (OK / FROZEN / DOWN), bitrate in and out, total. FRONT-1 frozen or gone (no new picture for 1 s) -> the front view switches to FRONT-2 by itself ("FRONT-1 LOST - showing FRONT-2"), and back when FRONT-1 has worked again for 2 s. A frozen picture always shows VIDEO FROZEN within 1 s. Remote driving warns if no front camera is live.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Measured in the simulation: about 135 ms on the boat LAN, ~190 ms over 4G (plus the camera's own delay, about 0.3-1 s for a Tapo - not measured). Camera setup, firmware updates (the "Camera internet 30 min" button, only from a station on board), wiring: gateway\README.md section 14, WIRING.md section 8.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: F. VIDEO RECORDING: RING BUFFER AND SAVE The gateway PC records all 4 cameras (full quality) all the time, in 1-minute files on its SSD. Only the last 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 60 minutes are kept (the "ring buffer", 60 minutes by default since step 13n4 = about 3.6 GB of the SSD; Cameras tab -> ring buffer, HELM or a station on board). Recording never uses the internet and never affects driving.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: KEEP 5' / 1h (the ●5' / ●1h buttons of a station, step 13n4): the last 5 / 60 minutes of all 4 cameras kept PERMANENTLY in <SSD>\video\events\ <id>\ ("keep": true in event.json): never deleted by the space rules below (also not once copied), the video NOT sent to the shore PC (only event.json). A shorter ring keeps what exists and says how much. A gateway installed BEFORE step 13n4 keeps the ring length it saved (state\recording.json, often 10 min): KEEP 1h then holds only 10 min - set the ring to 60 min once (Tools - Cameras - ring length).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The files of a SAVE / KEEP are linked by the gateway's background worker (within a second; never on its network loop, review 13n4b); on a drive without hard links they are copied only while the copy leaves the free-space margin.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: SAVE keeps 10 minutes before it + 2 minutes after it (all cameras), with: time, position, speed, heading, mode, alarms, what triggered it, and the name of the AURIX log file (record number) of that moment. A SAVE starts by:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * the SAVE button (Cameras tab; the big driver screen in part I), * the SAVE button on the boat's USB joystick (default: stick button 3; "Map buttons" in the Joystick tab) or on the shore PC's joystick (shore_joystick.json "save_button", default stick button 4 - step 13p; an older file keeps its own setting),

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * automatically: a new alarm (not "arrived"), a fault, the joystick taking over from HDG LOCK / AUTO / REMOTE / TRAINING, STANDBY because of a fault, slamming over the red limit (part H). Several triggers close together are one SAVE (it gets longer). VIEWERs can't SAVE. Where: <SSD>\video\events\YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_<trigger>\<CAMERA>\*.ts and event.json. The files play in VLC. Watch it next to the log: python logview.py -> "Open event..." (choose event.json: video + its log, cursor at the trigger) or "Video folder..."; choose the camera, click in the plots or press Play. Accuracy about 1 s.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: SSD space (1 hour of video from 4 Tapo C310 at full quality is about 3-4 GB, 4 x ~2 Mbit/s - check "GB/h" in the Cameras tab with the real cameras): when the SSD runs low the gateway PC deletes, in this order:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 1. the oldest ring buffer files, 2. the oldest SAVEs that are already copied to the shore PC (part G), but NEVER a SAVE that is not on the shore PC yet and NEVER a KEEP 5' / 1h. If that is not enough: STORAGE FULL (alarm GATEWAY STORAGE on the boat): new SAVEs are refused, the ring buffer keeps running. Free space: sync to the shore PC, or copy the events away and delete them. A camera that stops recording (cable, power) is restarted every few seconds; the others keep recording. "not recording: ..." shows it.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: G. SYNC TO THE SHORE PC The gateway PC copies its SSD to the shore PC by itself, over the VPN, whenever the boat is on 4G / 4G SIM 2 / RF (NEVER on STARLINK). In this order: 1. black box / alarms AURIX logs with an alarm, fault or SAVE in them, and every SAVE's description (event.json)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 2. event logs the audit log (who did what), log gaps 3. telemetry logs all other AURIX logs 4. saved events the SAVE video 5. ring video only if switched on (recording.ring_sync) - OFF * It only uses spare bandwidth: it measures its own ping to the shore and slows down at once when the link starts to queue (video, telemetry and commands stay fast). During REMOTE MANUAL it stops completely.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * A broken connection continues where it stopped (checked with SHA-256). * A file counts as "synced" only after the shore PC has checked it. Sync never deletes anything; only when the SSD runs low does the gateway PC delete SYNCED data (part F).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Network tab: SYNC state, speed, ping, what is waiting per class, the last confirmed file; on the shore PC also what it has received. The files arrive on the shore PC in <folder>\trygons-c2\ (same layout: aurix_logs, audit, video\events) - open them with logview.py. Setup: gateway\README.md section 16.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: H. SLAMMING (hull impacts) AND AUTOMATIC THROTTLE REDUCTION A BNO085 motion sensor measures the vertical acceleration about 200 times a second. Shown and logged: the hardest impact (g), impacts per minute, and the "level" (running average of the impacts; it falls again when the water gets smooth).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: YELLOW level above 70 % of the limit: warning beep; the forward throttle is reduced one step (10 %) at once and again every 5 s while it stays yellow (never below 30 %)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: RED one impact harder than the limit (default 3.0 g): red alarm SLAMMING, one more step down at once, and a video SAVE. The power limit STAYS (setting slam_red_reset = 0, "STEP", the default): a sudden drop to 30 % can be dangerous in a following sea (a wave from behind). slam_red_reset = 1 ("LIMIT_RESET") brings back the old behaviour: the power limit also drops to 30 %, like for every other alarm.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: It only ever REDUCES the throttle, in every mode (MANUAL, HDG LOCK, AUTO, REMOTE). The throttle comes down at its normal rate. POWER BACK ONLY WITH THE CAPTAIN'S ACCEPT (owner 2026-10-31, step 13q4): the reduction NEVER goes away by itself. After 30 s of calm water the boat asks on the captain's screen 1: "Calmer sea – restore power to 60 %?" [ACCEPT] [REJECT]

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: (60 = the throttle when the reduction began). ACCEPT = the power comes back gradually, at the normal throttle up rate; new impacts while it rises = it stops and is reduced again. REJECT, or no answer in 10 s = it stays reduced; a framed RESTORE POWER button stays in the screen 1 bottom bar and in the screen 2 control panel while the sea is calm, and the boat asks again after the next 2 minutes of calm water. Only the captain (or a single operator) can answer - a copilot can't (gateway code 118). In AUTO the boat gets its speed back only after the ACCEPT.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: After a reset there is no reduction (the boat starts in STANDBY with the startup power limit anyway). In AUTO, slamming also counts as rough water (the boat slows its target speed, chapter 7). OVERRIDE (only with the joystick on board, never the remote driver): "kick-down" - ease the throttle off (below 85 %), then push it to full and hold 1 s. The reduction is lifted (warning beep, "OVERRIDE" shown) until you go below the reduced value again. The power limit still applies. Staying at full throttle all the time never overrides. The limit: parameter slam_limit_g (1-8 g); the RED action: parameter slam_red_reset (0 = STEP, 1 = LIMIT_RESET).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The captain proposes, the driver confirms on the driver screen (part I). Sensor not working: "slamming sensor lost" warning, no reduction, the boat drives on normally. In the log: every impact as a SLAM event (peak, level, rate, reduction).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: I. TWO MONITORS: CAPTAIN SCREEN AND DRIVER SCREEN The normal ground-station window is the CAPTAIN screen (everything). The button "Driver screen" (top bar) opens the DRIVER screen - put it on the second monitor (Windows menu or Ctrl+Shift+2) and make it full size (F11). It is the full-screen camera HUD of chapter 5B: the FRONT camera fills the window (FRONT-2 by itself if FRONT-1 is lost; VIDEO FROZEN within 1 s; "NO FRONT CAMERA" while driving remotely without a live front camera), everything else is drawn on top of it.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: CAPTAIN ACTIONS THAT CHANGE THE DRIVING (mode, AUTO start / pause / resume / skip, heading +-1/10, sea state, training, parameters such as slam_limit_g, power-limit code) are only sent when the driver presses ACCEPT on the driver screen. THE GATEWAY ENFORCES THIS (not only the screen): it holds the action and asks the driver screen itself.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: no driver screen open REFUSED "driver screen not open"

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: driver presses REJECT REFUSED "rejected by the driver"

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: no answer within 10 s REFUSED "no answer from the driver"

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: driver screen closed / crashed REFUSED "driver screen lost" (the driver screen tells the gateway every second that it is open)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: STANDBY, "Lower now", alarm ack and HELM never wait. SINGLE-OPERATOR MODE (one person alone at the station): button "Single operator" (screen 2, HELM / roles panel) -> a warning -> ON. A purple banner on both screens shows it; the gateway logs it. Every driving action then needs YOUR confirmation in a small window (SEND / Cancel, 10 s). It switches OFF by itself when this station disconnects (also after a crash); press the button again to switch it off. The USB laptop on the boat (no gateway) is the service link: there the driver window asks when it is open, otherwise the action goes directly.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The window places (monitor, size) of screen 1, screen 2 and the tools window are remembered (gs_layout.json) and come back at the next start. F12 (or Ctrl+Tab) swaps screen 1 and screen 2 between the monitors.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: J. AIS: OTHER SHIPS (RECEIVE ONLY) The gateway PC listens to AIS (no transponder: other ships do NOT see us on AIS). Receiver: a USB AIS receiver on the gateway PC with its own VHF/AIS antenna. The AURIX never sees AIS - the gateway PC decodes it:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * position reports Class A (big ships) and Class B (small craft), * name, size, type, destination (static data). Each ship shows its age; with no new position it becomes STALE after 3 min (Class A) / 6 min (Class B) and disappears after 15 min. Between reports the position is predicted from speed and course. Wrong data is ignored (bad checksum, impossible jumps). AIS RECEIVER SILENT (alarm, warning only): no AIS message for 5 minutes while at sea (moving or in a driving mode). Check the antenna cable and the receiver. It never changes the mode or the power limit. ONLINE AIS (AISHub, wider area): OFF by default; only on 4G / RF, NEVER on STARLINK.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Ships seen by our own receiver keep our data when it is newer. SECOND GPS: if the AIS device has its own GPS (a future Class B transponder, or $GPRMC from the receiver), the gateway PC can send it to the AURIX as a second, independent GPS: setting ais.second_gps = true on the gateway PC AND parameter gps2_check_m (e.g. 30) on the boat. A main GPS more than that far from the second one is not trusted (spoofing). Tested: drags of 0.2 m/s and slower are NOT found by the other checks within 10 minutes, the second GPS finds them at 30 m. Both OFF by default.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: GPS TRUSTED AGAIN AFTER A SPOOF: 60 good fixes in a row (1 per second) that agree with dead reckoning. At speed the dead reckoning speed can be off (e.g. 15 % with fouling or a head sea, no paddlewheel); then:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * with the second GPS switched on, or with a paddlewheel: the GPS may differ from dead reckoning ALONG the course by DR's speed error -> trusted again after about 60 s; * with neither: only when GPS and dead reckoning agree - this can take several minutes at speed (AUTO goes on by dead reckoning, slower, and holds the heading at the DR limit). It can't safely be faster: a spoofer dragging the position slowly along the course looks exactly like a wrong speed estimate.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Across the course nothing is relaxed: a GPS pulled sideways is never trusted again. AIS DOES NOT SHOW small boats, jet skis, swimmers, kayaks or anything without a transponder. The lookout on board and the cameras stay essential. K. DEPTH CHARTS AND SEA MARKS (OFFLINE) NOT FOR NAVIGATION - free data, may be inaccurate near the coast. This note is always on the map. Use the official charts and your eyes. Area: Saronic Gulf, the Attica coast around Sounion, the South Euboean Gulf, Kea / Makronisos, with a margin (charts\areas.json - add more areas there). Depth: EMODnet Bathymetry (about 115 m grid, depth below the lowest tide), sea marks (buoys, beacons, lights, harbours): OpenSeaMap.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: Gaps can be filled from a GEBCO grid. Their names are shown on the map (the licences require it). MAKE THE CHARTS ONCE (needs internet, about 10 minutes): C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\python.exe tools\chartprep.py

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: -> charts\attica\ (depth.bin, contours.json, seamarks.json, area.json). Copy that folder to the gateway PC too (gateway\README.md section 18): the gateway PC uses it for the shallow-water checks. After that the map works with NO internet. Map (screen 2), View menu: Depth (shading: dark = shallow, white = deep, sand = land), Contours (2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 m), Sea marks, AIS ships, Range rings - each on / off. Zoom out up to 400 m per pixel. The driver screen's small map shows the same, 3 km wide. On the map, everywhere the data has no depth (land, harbours, very close to the coast) counts as SHALLOW for every check (part L).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: L. SHALLOW WATER Limit = the larger of 3.0 m and (draft + margin). SET THEM ON THE GATEWAY PC (gateway.json "shallow"): draft_m = from the water line to the lowest point of the outboard with the leg DOWN (measure it!), margin_m = how much water you want under it (1 m), shallow_m = at least this (3 m). The ground station shows the limit (Program tab profile, red line). AUTO PROGRAMS (Program tab):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * "Check depth": every leg must stay over water deeper than the limit and not pass closer than 50 m to shallower water. A bad leg is shown: the message gives the leg and the position, a red X on the map, the depth profile (red = too shallow).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: * Upload and AUTO start / resume through the gateway are REFUSED the same way by the gateway PC ("shallow water on the route: leg ... at lat lon"), also the leg from the boat to the waypoint at AUTO start. Without charts on the gateway PC AUTO is refused ("no depth charts").

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: WHILE DRIVING (any mode): if the boat will be over shallow water within the next 30 s (at least 200 m ahead) -> "SHALLOW WATER AHEAD" on both screens. In AUTO the boat also slows to 4 kn and the SHALLOW WATER alarm sounds. In MANUAL / HDG LOCK / REMOTE it is a warning only: you steer. Every collision-avoidance route (part M) passes the same depth check. The charts are free data and NOT FOR NAVIGATION: near the coast, in harbours and where there is no data, "no data" counts as shallow. How AUTO is slowed: the gateway PC sends a "navigation request" twice a second (speed cap, avoidance heading, alarms) that the boat applies only in AUTO.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: If the gateway PC goes quiet in the middle of such a request, the boat holds its heading, slows to 4 kn (parameter nav_lost_kn) and sounds COLLISION RISK - DRIVER DECISION. Joystick and STANDBY always win.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: M. COLLISION AVOIDANCE (AIS SHIPS) AIS DOES NOT SHOW small boats, jet skis, swimmers, kayaks, divers or anything without a transponder, and a ship's AIS can be wrong, late or switched off. Collision avoidance helps with BIG ships only. KEEP A LOOKOUT. A radar reflector on the boat helps big ships see YOU. The gateway PC computes for every AIS ship the CPA (how close it will pass) and the TCPA (in how many minutes):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: WARNING CPA under 0.5 nm within 10 min (yellow on the maps)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: DANGER CPA under 0.25 nm within 6 min (red on the maps + the driver screen; alarm COLLISION RISK, video SAVE)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: (gateway PC settings gateway.json "avoid": warn_nm, warn_min, danger_nm, danger_min, safe_nm, clear_nm, min_kn ...) WHAT HAPPENS IN EACH MODE:

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: AUTO automatic, step by step, already at the WARNING level (early, while there is still room):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 1. slow down (half speed, at least 4 kn) and re-check after 20 s; 2. still too close -> a route that passes ASTERN of the ship (starboard turns first, then port; it never crosses ahead of a ship's bow, keeps 0.5 nm, and passes the depth check of part L). The route is drawn on both maps.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 3. clear (going back is safe) -> the boat rejoins its leg. Every decision is written to the gateway PC's audit log.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: HDG LOCK at the WARNING level too: the same route as a PROPOSAL on the driver screen ("Steer 074 and slow to 4 kn?") - ACCEPT changes the locked heading, REJECT keeps it (no new proposal for 60 s, the alarm stays). When clear: "Back to heading 344?" (ACCEPT / REJECT). The throttle stays with you. Only the driver screen (or the captain in SINGLE-OPERATOR mode) can answer. UNCREWED HDG LOCK (owner 2026-11-01): NO proposal and NO turn - the boat only slows down (DRIVER DECISION when it can't be solved: the slowest speed).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: MANUAL / REMOTE MANUAL alarm only: you steer.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: COLLISION RISK - DRIVER DECISION: the situation can't be solved safely by the gateway PC (two or more dangerous ships, a ship that is turning, old / stale AIS data, no safe route): in AUTO the boat slows to 4 kn and KEEPS ITS COURSE (never an unchecked route). YOU decide: take the joystick. The boat only applies what the gateway PC asks in AUTO (or after your ACCEPT in HDG LOCK), and only within all its own rules (power limit, joystick wins, STANDBY wins).
