If the gateway PC goes silent during an avoidance, the boat holds its heading, slows to 4 kn and sounds DRIVER DECISION.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: The boat also checks the gateway PC's request itself: an avoidance heading must come with a speed reduction, and one more than 150 deg off the leg (parameter nav_max_dev) is not steered (the boat slows, DRIVER DECISION); an accepted HDG LOCK heading counts only if it came while HDG LOCK was on. Collision and shallow-water alarms do NOT lower the power limit (slowing down is done by the speed request itself). Screen 2, tab "AIS": the ship list (name, distance, bearing, CPA, TCPA, age), click a ship for its details.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: N. OBSTACLE DETECTION WITH THE FRONT CAMERA (eWaSR, AI) The gateway PC looks at the front camera (FRONT-1, FRONT-2 after a switch-over) with a small AI model (eWaSR) that colours every part of the picture as WATER, SKY or OBSTACLE. Things sitting on the water (boats, buoys, swimmers, rocks) become obstacles with a bearing and a ROUGH distance. IT NEVER STEERS THE BOAT AND NEVER GIVES MORE THROTTLE. It does not see everything (night, fog, glare, small things far away): keep a lookout. Licence: model and code Apache-2.0, test pictures MaSTr1325 CC BY 4.0 - both allowed for this project (gateway\vision\README.md). STAGES (screen 2, Tools - Cameras; every change is logged):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 1 overlay + log (ON) colours over the front camera on the driver screen, boxes with bearing + "~120 m (rough)", orange sectors on the maps, a log file

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 2 alarm + SAVE (ON) an obstacle in the path ahead (only while driving, not moored in STANDBY): alarm OBSTACLE AHEAD + video SAVE. No effect on the boat.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: 3 slows AUTO (OFF) AUTO slows to 3 kn (idle when nearer than 40 m); HDG LOCK: "slow down" on the driver screen (the throttle stays yours); MANUAL / REMOTE: alarm only. Switch it on ONLY after sea trials; the driver screen must ACCEPT it.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: An obstacle must be seen in 3 pictures in a row before it counts (wakes, foam and glare flicker and are filtered). The bottom of the picture (own bow, own wake) is ignored. DRIVER SCREEN: "VISION ACTIVE 2.0" in the bottom line; the overlay on / off and its opacity in the AR menu (key O = overlay on / off); the button "CLEAR SLOWDOWN" appears while a STAGE 3 slowdown is active. STATUS (a notice, never an alarm, never a mode change):

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: PAUSED the gateway PC's main jobs need the CPU, or its CPU is hot / throttling

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: DEGRADED too slow (below 1 picture / s) or the camera gives no pictures

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: OFFLINE switched off, model missing, crashed (it restarts by itself)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: THE IDEA
passages.text: If vision stops working while it slows AUTO down, the slowdown STAYS until the driver presses CLEAR SLOWDOWN (it is never released by itself). It runs on the gateway PC's CPU (no NVIDIA; measured load: gateway\README.md section 21). Setup and the model file: gateway\vision\README.md. Your own recordings can be tested on the PC: tools\bin\vision-python\python.exe gateway\vision\evaluate.py FILE.ts -> test_results\vision_eval\report.md (speed, detections, pictures). Samples for an own Saronic dataset (picture + mask) can be switched on (vision.samples on the gateway PC); they use at most 500 MB.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: Talk with anyone near the boat - swimmers, fishing boats, divers, the coast guard - through a horn speaker on the boat, and listen to its microphone. There is NO VHF radio. The loudhailer is its own program on the gateway PC (a USB sound card -> amplifier -> horn; an outdoor microphone): it NEVER touches the AURIX, the driving or the alarms. If it fails you get a notice ("LOUDHAILER OFF"), never an alarm or a mode change; it restarts by itself. TALK (Greek ΟΜΙΛΙΑ): a framed SCREEN button - press and HOLD while you speak, let go when you are done.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: It is on the bottom bar of screen 1, on bar 2 of screen 2 (the copilot's PC too) and on Tools - Loudhailer. It is NOT on the joystick. One person at a time: the gateway gives the horn to whoever pressed FIRST; everybody else sees a grey TALK button and "SPEAKING: CAPTAIN" (or COPILOT) - on screen 2 at the start of the message line. The CAPTAIN is the exception (owner 2026-11-04): the captain's TALK takes the horn AT ONCE from anyone talking; that station sees THE CAPTAIN TOOK THE HORN (a sound signal already playing still ends first). While anyone talks the boat microphone is switched off (no echo / howling).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: A press ends by itself after 2 minutes (a stuck button) or 1 s without voice (a lost link).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: LISTEN: the boat microphone plays on this PC's headset / speakers all the time (Tools - Loudhailer: mute, volume here, a white level meter; screen 1 shows "BOAT MIC" and its level). It is silent while someone talks. READY MESSAGES: one click = the message spoken in Greek, then in English (this PC's offline voice, Tools - Sound), e.g. "Unmanned vessel - keep clear". Edit the list on the Tools page (add / save / delete / back to the default list); it is kept on this PC.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: SOUND SIGNALS: "DANGER - 5 short blasts" and "1 prolonged blast", made on the boat (they take the horn for their time). VOLUME: the horn's volume can be set by the HELM station or a station on the boat, never above the LIMIT on the gateway (gateway.json "loudhailer": "volume_max_pct", default 80 %, 0..100). The % is a LINEAR gain of the voice samples, not a loudness: set the real loudness with the amplifier's trimmer so that 80 % is safe for a swimmer close to the boat.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: SOUND CARD: the gateway uses ONLY the sound card named in gateway.json "loudhailer": "out_dev" / "in_dev" - without them (or with "" / "default") the loudhailer stays OFF ("speaker / microphone not configured"), never the gateway PC's own speaker or microphone. (The simulator / demo needs none.)

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: THE LINK: voice is small (~33 kbit/s, ~45 kbit/s on the wire). It ranks above the copilot's camera view but below the captain's driving data and video: on a weak / busy link the voice to that station stops first ("VOICE OFF (weak link)"); with the data saver only the captain keeps it. The latency is shown on the Tools page.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: LOUDHAILER AND BOAT MICROPHONE (step 13r, owner 2026-11-02)
passages.text: RECORDING: both directions are recorded on the gateway SSD together with the cameras (video/ring/AUDIO, 1-minute WAV files) and are inside every SAVE, 5' and 1h (folder AUDIO next to the camera folders, same time window). DEMO / SIMULATOR: a simulated horn + microphone (sea noise; a 'contact' answers now and then) - nothing on this PC's sound card on the boat side. Hardware: PARTS.md (loudhailer) and WIRING.md section 3G.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - REGISTRATION
passages.text: Six small camera drones are stacked in the boat under a hatch (slot 1 = the top one = the next out). OBSERVATION ONLY: no payload, no release - the gateway's MAVLink allow-list has no such command at all. Tools - UAV magazine shows the 6 slots with the UAV picture: name, sysid, ArduPilot version, battery, GPS, video channel, ELRS radio, and READY or NOT launchable with the reason. REGISTER reads the drone through the slot's USB cable and checks it - READ ONLY: the gateway never changes a drone setting (set them with Mission Planner).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - REGISTRATION
passages.text: It refuses a drone with any output but its 4 motors, a gripper / parachute / winch / relay / mount / script / aux switch, the wrong failsafes, the RC receiver not ignored, a missing sensor or a duplicate sysid. A drone that is not registered or fails a check is never launched. While a drone is in its slot the gateway gives its GPS the time and the boat's position (warm start: a faster fix after the hatch opens). Any role but VIEWER may register. The UAV programs never touch the boat's driving or alarms; a failure is a notice only.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - ROUTES AND LAUNCH (step U3)
passages.text: Routes: draw the route on the map as usual and press "Send route". With a UAV magazine a box asks WHERE TO: THE BOAT (the normal AUTO route), NEXT UAV (slot n), a UAV in the magazine, or a FLYING UAV (it gets the new mission in the air; if the gateway refuses it, the old one goes on). A right click on the map: "Go here (the boat)" = a 2-point route from the boat to the point (every AUTO rule as usual) and "Send a UAV here". Every UAV point flies at 50 m.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - ROUTES AND LAUNCH (step U3)
passages.text: The gateway checks every UAV route: altitude 10..120 m, radio range (1500 m from the launch point and from the boat), battery with the landing reserve, the air no-fly zones and the air geofence (files on the gateway, not authoritative); a refusal says why. Each mission ends HOVERING over the last point - never a landing. Launch: Tools - UAV magazine - PREPARE LAUNCH (copilot or captain). The CAPTAIN answers YES / NO on screen 1 (a single operator answers his own).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - ROUTES AND LAUNCH (step U3)
passages.text: The launch goes WHEN THE COPILOT SAYS SO, at any boat speed or mode (owner 2026-11-04); above 5 kn every station shows HIGH SPEED - take-off risk (ΥΨΗΛΗ ΤΑΧΥΤΗΤΑ – κίνδυνος στην απογείωση): a warning only, slow down when you can. It needs a trusted GPS, no boat WARNING alarm, the relay board answering, a station holding HELM, the hatch healthy.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - ROUTES AND LAUNCH (step U3)
passages.text: Then, strictly from the top slot: mission loaded and read back, the hatch opens (its OPEN switch), GPS fix (no fix in 5 s: it climbs straight up to 15 m and waits there for GPS, at any boat speed), ARM, climb to 30 m (+5 m per slot), clear of the boat at 10 m, the next one at least 15 s later; after the last the hatch closes. ANY warning STOPS the launch: drones in the air go on with their missions, no further drone is armed, the hatch stays as it is.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - ROUTES AND LAUNCH (step U3)
passages.text: A drone that armed but did not climb is disarmed at once and the hatch stays OPEN: check the magazine, then HATCH CLOSE (the captain's own button). STOP LAUNCH stops it from any crew station. The hatch relay is shown as a lamp only - no station can switch it. Without a station holding HELM nothing can switch it ("HATCH NOT CLOSED - take HELM and close it").

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - MAP, TELEMETRY, VIDEO, AI (step U4)
passages.text: Every flying UAV is on screen 2's map with its picture (turned with its heading), its own dashed track and a label: UAV n, altitude, battery %, link % (amber = battery below 30 %, the battery minimum near, or a weak link). A click on a UAV opens its VIDEO full screen on screen 2 (bar 1 also lists the UAVs with a video; MAP / Esc = back) with its own green values (altitude, speed, battery, link, heading, distance to the boat).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - MAP, TELEMETRY, VIDEO, AI (step U4)
passages.text: The gateway records every UAV video in its ring (in every SAVE / KEEP 5' / 1 h) and sends it only to a station that has it OPEN - on DATA SAVER / STARLINK there is NO UAV video for anyone, and when the link is busy the UAV video goes before the captain's cameras. AI: the same obstacle detection ("AI") looks at the UAV videos that are open on a screen, one after the other, slowly (0.5 pictures a second in all), and only when the boat's own front camera AI does not need the computer. It only draws boxes and gives a notice - it never slows or steers the boat.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - MAP, TELEMETRY, VIDEO, AI (step U4)
passages.text: It was trained on views from a boat, not from the air: its boxes on a UAV picture may be poor. The ONLY landing: the battery minimum. The gateway watches every flying UAV: when the battery left is just enough to descend from where it is, it LANDS there (over the sea the drone is lost - the owner's rule). A CAUTION on every station 60 s and 20 s before ("UAV n LANDING IN 60 s - battery minimum") and at the landing. Lost radio link, no GPS or any warning = it holds / goes on with its mission, never a landing.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - MAP, TELEMETRY, VIDEO, AI (step U4)
passages.text: Notices (never boat alarms): UAV n LINK LOST / link back, UAV n towards the radio range limit, UAV n VIDEO LOST, UAV n BATTERY DATA STALE (its battery state not heard for 5 s: the gateway can't judge the battery minimum, only the drone's own battery backstop lands it), the UAV router OFFLINE (also on screen 1's notices). Flight logs: the gateway writes one file per flight (a line a second: position, altitude, speed, battery, link, mode). Tools - UAV magazine - FLIGHT LOGS, choose one, EXPORT CSV (a spreadsheet) or EXPORT GPX (Google Earth, OpenCPN).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: Who: the COPILOT may fly a UAV from his own station at any time (his joystick never drives the boat). The CAPTAIN only with the boat in STANDBY - while his joystick is on a UAV the boat gets nothing from it. How: open the UAV's video (a click on it on the map, or bar 1 of the camera view) and press FLY UAV n (also Tools - UAV magazine). CENTRE THE STICK first: until the gateway has seen it centred the UAV only holds.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: Then: stick forward / back / left / right = fly that way relative to the UAV's nose (up to 10 m/s), the TWCS lever = climb / descend (its middle 45-55 % = keep the altitude; a station without a lever keeps the altitude), the twist = turn. Let go = the UAV stops and holds its position. It never goes below 10 m or above 120 m, and it stops at the air geofence / a no-fly zone ("held: ..." on the screen). It is ASSISTED flying only - the joystick never works the drone's motors directly.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: The screens: "JOYSTICK -> UAV n" on both screens; screen 1 shows the UAV's video with its own green values (altitude, climb, speed, battery, link, heading, the distance + an ARROW to the boat) - the boat's mode, the MASTER lamps, the alarms and SAVE stay. RETURN TO BOAT (screen 1, bar 1 of the camera view, the UAV page) = the UAV hovers where it is and the joystick is back on the boat (it never means "fly back" - the drones never land on the boat).

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: While the captain flies: his driving commands and every copilot request that needs his ACCEPT are refused at once ("the joystick is on a UAV"); STANDBY, AUTO PAUSE and DP STOP always work. Questions on his screen are answered with the MOUSE only (the joystick buttons fly the drone). The boat leaving STANDBY ends it at once: the UAV hovers, the joystick is back on the boat. One pilot per UAV: the first one keeps it, another station is refused ("another pilot flies this UAV") - EXCEPT the CAPTAIN, who can take a UAV over from the copilot at once (owner decision): the copilot sees "THE CAPTAIN TOOK CONTROL" and the UAV holds during the hand-over.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: A copilot cannot take one from the captain. No joystick data for 0.5 s = the UAV holds; for 3 s (or the station disconnects) = manual control ends, the UAV hovers. Also: FLY is refused while the launch still owns the UAV (it climbs out of the hatch or waits for GPS) - wait until it flies its mission. While a UAV is flown by hand no new route is accepted for it ("give it back first"). When the UAV's own data is older than 1 s the stick moves nothing (it holds); a climb / descent into a no-fly zone's altitude band is stopped like a move towards its edge.

passages.chapter: THE GATEWAY (GATEWAY PC) AND REMOTE ACCESS
passages.heading: UAV MAGAZINE - FLYING A UAV BY HAND (step U5)
passages.text: A UAV without GPS that is given back holds its altitude (ALT_HOLD) instead of its position. When the captain takes a UAV, every question still open for his ACCEPT is refused at once.
* After EVERY power-up or reset: 30 % forward, 5 % reverse (of the full throttle travel). Never saved. * Raise, one step at a time (30 -> 50 -> 75 -> 100 %; reverse 5 -> 10 -> 15):

1. "Raise fwd" (or "Raise rev") in the ground station, 2. type the 4-digit code the window shows, "Send code", 3. press CONFIRM on the joystick within 10 s (stick centred). Each step needs the whole sequence again. Wrong / old code: refused.

* It drops back to 30 / 5 AT ONCE on: "Lower now", TAKE or a stick takeover, the STANDBY button, ANY alarm (incl. PC link lost, GPS lost, compass / joystick / gear fault), entering TRAINING, and after 2 min below 3 kn. The throttle then comes down at its normal rate (no sudden cut), but it can never go above the new limit. * In AUTO the leg speed is limited by it; the window shows "SPEED LIMITED BY POWER LIMIT". * Enforced in the lowest layer: app/servo.c, the only code that drives the throttle servo. The CPU1 monitor checks it again.

COMPASS LOST, GPS LOST, GPS SUSPECT (spoof flag, jump, speed, course, slow drag, second GPS, or a fix with impossible numbers - NaN, latitude beyond 90, ...), DEAD RECKONING LIMIT, ARRIVAL UNCERTAIN, ARRIVED, GEAR FAULT, TRAINING, JOYSTICK FAULT, JOYSTICK NOT CENTRED, JOYSTICK TOOK CONTROL, PC LINK LOST
NOT NEUTRAL AT START outputs not armed: gear not in neutral / stick held SAFETY MONITOR TRIPPED CPU1 forced idle + neutral (see chapter 12)
EMERGENCY STOP the e-stop switch is pressed: STANDBY, nothing else until it is released (chapter 6A)
CONTROL LOOP OVERRUN a control cycle took longer than 50 ms
LOG FAILURE SD card missing / full / failing (control goes on)
GATEWAY LOST the gateway PC is silent for 3 s (no mode change)
SHALLOW WATER AUTO: shallow water ahead (charts); the boat slows to 4 kn (part L)
COLLISION RISK an AIS ship will pass closer than 0.25 nm within 6 min (part M); AUTO avoids it, HDG LOCK proposes
OBSTACLE AHEAD the front camera sees an obstacle in the path (part N, STAGE 2 / 3); a warning - only STAGE 3 slows AUTO
COLLISION RISK - DRIVER DECISION the gateway PC can't solve it safely (or went silent during an avoidance): slow, keep course - YOU decide (part M)
AIS RECEIVER SILENT no AIS message for 5 min at sea: antenna / receiver (warning only, part J)

SLAMMING an impact harder than slam_limit_g: throttle reduced one step, video SAVE; the power limit stays (only with slam_red_reset = 1 it drops to 30 %); power back ONLY with the captain's ACCEPT (part H)
GATEWAY STORAGE the gateway PC's SSD is missing / failing, or STORAGE FULL (no mode change; SAVE refused while full)
REMOTE LINK LOST the remote station holding HELM disappeared; HELM goes back to nobody (no mode change)
CHANNEL FALLBACK the internet channel you chose (MANUAL) failed; the gateway uses the next working one (no mode change)
REMOTE DRIVING LINK LOST remote joystick data too old / missing: idle, neutral, gyro heading hold; STANDBY after 5 s

LOW BATTERY the 12 V bank (filtered over ~30 s) stayed below batt_low_v (11.8 V, TO CONFIRM) for 60 s; clears 0.3 V higher. ADVISORY: no mode change, the power limit STAYS (the way home may need the power), no video SAVE. The acknowledge clears it once the bank is back above 12.1 V. (In the log / telemetry it is bit 1 of the SECOND alarm word, alarm_bits2: the first word is full.) Not measured at all (divider not wired, converter dead): the NOTICE "NO VOLTAGE DATA" after 5 s - no alarm, nothing else changes.

RELAY BOARD SILENT the relay board gave no valid reply for 3 s (RS485) / its node 30 silent, not OPERATIONAL, ERROR or the CAN bus down (DroneCAN board, step 11f) while a relay table is loaded. ADVISORY: states shown unknown, no new relay command; no mode change, the power limit stays, no buzzer. Clears by itself when the board answers (second alarm word, bit 2). Never shown without a fitted relay board.

DP THRUSTER HOT a DP thruster used its heat budget (boat file run_s): it stays at 0 until it rested (rest_s). An ordinary alarm (buzzer, power limit back to 30 / 5). In DP the DP ends (thrusters 0, STANDBY: it can't hold with one thruster); no new DP until it rested. The acknowledge keeps it while the thruster is still hot (second alarm word, bit 3).

DP OFF SPOT DP SPOT / JOG: the boat is farther than spot_alarm_m (boat file, 15 m) from the spot. ADVISORY: DP keeps trying, the power limit stays; more than 50 m or 2 min off -> thrusters 0, STANDBY (second word, bit 4).
DP OVERPOWER both DP thrusters at their limit for 10 s: the wind / current is too strong. ADVISORY (bit 5).

CAN NODE LOST (DroneCAN servo nodes, only when a CAN bus is fitted) a REQUIRED node (throttle 20 / steering 21 / gear 22) sent no heartbeat for 1.5 s, is not OPERATIONAL, reports ERROR / CRITICAL, or REBOOTED (its uptime went back), or the bus is dead. An ordinary alarm (buzzer, power limit 30 / 5) + STANDBY (idle + neutral first); no mode but STANDBY while a required node is lost or not seen yet. A rebooted node stays lost until it ran 2 s and you acknowledge in STANDBY. The relay board node (30) is only shown, never this alarm. A node reporting WARNING = a notice only. (Second alarm word, bit 6.)

CAN BUS FAULT the CAN bus is off / error passive for more than 100 ms (cable, termination, every node unpowered, transceiver), the CAN controller did not start, or a frame FROM OUR OWN NODE ID 10 is on the bus: the old Pixhawk is still connected - it is node 10 too and must NEVER be on the bus with the AURIX (WIRING.md 3E). Same reaction as CAN NODE LOST; it clears 3 s after the last such frame. A node asking for a dynamic node ID (no fixed ID set) = a notice only - set its ID with the DroneCAN GUI Tool.

(Second word, bit 7.) The node table (health, mode, uptime, reboots, counters) is on the Bench page of the USB laptop. The servos over CAN (step 11e, chapter 12) stay off on the board (HAL_CAN_FITTED / HAL_CAN_SERVOS 0) until the kit's CAN pins are confirmed.

GEOFENCE BREACH UNCREWED HDG LOCK only (owner 2026-11-01): the gateway says the boat is outside the geofence -> STANDBY (idle + neutral first). It stays while the gateway still reports the boat outside. (Second word, bit 8.)

Every new alarm drops the power limit to 30 / 5 and starts a black-box file (except the navigation warnings SHALLOW WATER, COLLISION RISK, DRIVER DECISION, OBSTACLE AHEAD, AIS RECEIVER SILENT, LOW BATTERY, RELAY BOARD SILENT, DP OFF SPOT and DP OVERPOWER: they never change the power limit; RELAY BOARD SILENT doesn't sound the boat's buzzer and doesn't block a power raise either). Acknowledge: STANDBY button in STANDBY, or "ACK ALARM" in the ALARMS panel (top right of screen 2). Both screens list every active alarm in ONE place (screen 1: under the right mirror; screen 2: top right), one per line, most severe first; an alarm not yet acknowledged on THIS PC flashes, the others are steady.

An acknowledge clears only the alarms whose cause is gone: a compass / GPS / joystick fault, a lost link, a tripped monitor, a gateway problem ... that is still there stays on (from any station, also from shore).
ON THE PC every alarm has a LEVEL (sounds, lamps: chapters 5B / 5D):

WARNING COMPASS LOST, GEAR FAULT, JOYSTICK FAULT, SAFETY MONITOR TRIPPED, REMOTE DRIVING LINK LOST, COLLISION RISK (+ DRIVER DECISION), SHALLOW WATER, EMERGENCY STOP, CAN NODE LOST, CAN BUS FAULT, NO DATA FROM THE BOAT

ADVISORY ARRIVED, TRAINING, JOYSTICK TOOK CONTROL, AIS RECEIVER SILENT, LOW BATTERY, RELAY BOARD SILENT (groundstation\alerts.py). The GENERAL WARNING / CAUTION lamps of the driver screen only silence this PC - they are not the boat's ALARM ACK.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.text: * Gear changes only at idle: idle -> wait -> neutral -> wait -> gear. * Every fault / STANDBY: idle + neutral FIRST, then steering held (the DroneCAN position servo: HOLD). Idle is commanded AT ONCE; neutral once the throttle servo must be at idle (thr_trav_s); until idle + neutral the onboard stick (from MANUAL) or the gyro (from REMOTE, or a joystick fault) keeps steering. Compass lost while moving (AUTO / TRAINING): gyro steering until stopped (or outboard to centre if the gyro is gone too). In HDG LOCK: gyro hold, the throttle stays with you; STANDBY once you have stopped. In MANUAL: alarm only.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.text: * Throttle rate limits; reverse limited; the power limit (chapter 10). * The joystick always wins; the STANDBY button always wins. * NEUTRAL-START INTERLOCK: after power-up the outputs only arm when the throttle is idle, neutral is confirmed (neutral switch if fitted) and the stick is centred - and the joystick must be there: no joystick seen (not plugged in, USB bridge not sending yet) = not armed, alarm NOT NEUTRAL AT START. Until then: STANDBY only, alarm after 3 s.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.text: * WATCHDOGS on all three cores (100 ms on core 0). A stuck loop resets the chip: everything starts again in STANDBY at 30 %. * CPU1 SAFETY MONITOR: checks every 1 ms, on its own: throttle above the power limit, gear moving with the throttle open, core 0 silent for 200 ms. Then it forces idle + neutral + alarm, the steering servo HOLDS its position, and P10.5 opens the engine kill circuit ONLY in UNCREWED; core 0 can't undo it until a reset. Reaction in the simulator: 10-20 ms (one check), 220 ms for a frozen core 0.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.text: * Heading hold pauses (outboard held still) when there is no propulsion, so the angle estimate can't drift while you are stopped. * Logging can never block control (chapter 13).

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: The boat's throttle, steering and gear servos can be DroneCAN nodes (throttle 20, steering 21 = a 360 deg position servo, gear 22). The code for it is complete and tested in the simulator ("autopilot_sim all --can" = worst-case servos, throttle 6 s / steering 12 s lock to lock; "all --can-fast" = 2 s / 3 s). On the board it stays OFF (hal/hal_pins.h HAL_CAN_FITTED 0 and HAL_CAN_SERVOS 0) until the owner has checked the kit's CAN pins and the servo nodes on the bench (FIRST_TEST.md 3j). What changes with the DroneCAN servos:

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * Throttle UP is gentle (15 %/s), DOWN is faster (50 %/s); STANDBY, the e-stop, a lost link, a lost node, every fault and a monitor trip command IDLE AT ONCE (no rate limit - only the servo's own speed).

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * "Idle" for every rule that waits for it (gear change, steering hold, ENGINE KILL, STARTER, generator, DP, restart) = where the throttle servo MUST be by now: the software assumes the slowest servo (thr_trav_s, 6 s from full to idle). The gear servo moves only after that. A longer thr_trav_s is taken at once (STANDBY); a SHORTER one needs a joystick CONFIRM (it is logged) and is never saved.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * After every boot the first command is THROTTLE IDLE; the gear gets no command for the throttle travel time; the steering gets NO command until a mode steers (no automatic centring). After a power-on the steering position is unknown: the first moves run at the worst-case speed without play compensation.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * Lost commands (reset, bus fault, a dead AURIX): every servo HOLDS where it is. The throttle comes down by the AURIX (idle first after a boot), by CPU1's safe frames, or the engine is stopped (kill cord / e-stop / UNCREWED dead-man).

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * Throttle node lost: the gear is HELD (never an automatic neutral); CREWED = alarm + STANDBY; UNCREWED = ENGINE KILL at once (owner decision OD-3, the one exception to "kill only after idle + neutral"). * Monitor trip: CPU1 sends its own safe frames every 20 ms (throttle idle, steering held, gear held until the throttle travel time, then neutral while the throttle node works); core 0's frames are cancelled. The servo power is never cut. Core 0's 10 ms actuator task stopping for 100 ms is a trip too (MON_TRIP_CAN_TX).

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * The e-stop stops the ENGINE in every profile (hard-wired kill circuit contact, WIRING.md); the software ENGINE KILL stays UNCREWED only. * UNCREWED dead-man: a timer relay in the kill circuit, held "run" by pulses from CPU1 (P10.5, ~1.5 s): no pulses = the engine stops by itself (trip, frozen AURIX, throttle node lost, kill latched). Part, time and arming switch: TO CONFIRM (WIRING.md 3A). A warm reset in UNCREWED may stop the engine (the pulses restart only after the profile detection) - TO CONFIRM.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * STEERING TRAINING for the position servo (TRAINING, from STANDBY, slow ahead in calm water): centre, small steps, large steps, a reversal staircase, a check run - it measures the servo speed per direction, the play (backlash), the turn gain K and the boat's time constant. Accept = saved in data-flash slot 5 (format 2; an old DC-motor result is refused: "NV DATA RESET" + "TRAINING NEEDED"). Without TRAINING the steering uses the worst-case speed and no play compensation.

passages.chapter: SAFETY RULES BUILT INTO THE SOFTWARE
passages.heading: DRONECAN SERVOS (STEP 11e - THE CODE IS READY, THE BOARD STILL USES PWM)
passages.text: * With TRAINING: every direction change adds the measured play, the command never moves faster than the servo, and in steady calm-water HDG LOCK / AUTO the model adapts slowly (RAM only, K / tau within 0.7 - 1.3 x TRAINING, the play only smaller, the speed never faster). On any doubt (sensor fault, node lost, a bound reached, a large model error) it goes back to the TRAINING values at once: notice STEERING MODEL RESET. The Control page shows the stored / adapted values, the confidence, the last reset reason and the throttle model.

Full details and pin tables: WIRING.md. Everything is 3.3 V - NEVER 5 V. Joystick (A0 / A1 + D2 TAKE, D3 AUTO, D4 CONFIRM), panel buttons on the Shield2Go connectors (STANDBY P00.4, HDG LOCK P10.8, -1 P23.4, +1 P23.5, -10 P32.2, +10 P32.3), throttle servo D9, gear servo D8, steering motor driver D6 / D7, safety relay D10, neutral switch D5, microSD click in the mikroBUS socket, PC on the USB cable. Gateway PC: P15.0 (TX) -> RXD, P15.1 (RX) <- TXD, GND of a 3.3 V TTL USB-UART adapter (NEVER RS232). USB joystick bridge: Teensy pin 1 (TX) -> P20.3 (Shield2Go 2, ASCLIN3 RX), GND to GND, own 5 V supply.
SHOPPING LIST: PARTS.md (one list for everything: boat electronics, gateway, cameras, sensors, USB joystick, AIS, shore PC).
Defaults: sb_default_config() in app/smallboat.c (+ gear.c, throttle.c, joystick.c, powerlim.c, servo.c). (PC) = also in the Config tab.
Power limit 30 % fwd / 5 % rev at start; steps 50/75/100; reverse max 15; drop after 2 min below 3 kn
Throttle servo 1000 us = idle, 2000 us = full (calibrate!)
Gear servo pulses F 1900 us, N 1500 us, R 1100 us
Gear waits idle 1.0 s, neutral 1.0 s, engage 0.8 s

Throttle +15 %/s up (thr_up_pc_s, 2..30), -50 %/s down (thr_dn_pc_s, 20..200), reverse max 30 %; STANDBY / faults / trip: idle AT ONCE; the servo travel for every "idle" wait 6 s (thr_trav_s, 1..30: longer at once, shorter only with a CONFIRM, RAM only)
Joystick deadband 15 % (PC), engage 0.1 s, full stick = 100 % demand (PC; the power limit applies)
USB joystick neutral zone 45-55 %, lever override 10 %, pickup window 3 % (Joystick tab, saved); frame timeout 150 ms, > 5 CRC errors / s, counter stuck 3 frames, start-up grace 5 s
AUTO max leg speed 25 kn (PC), slow from 150 m (PC), approach 4 kn (PC), leg 10 m .. 50 km

Battery (12 V bank) LOW BATTERY below batt_low_v 11.8 V (PC, 10..13.5, TO CONFIRM) for 60 s, clears 0.3 V higher; filters ~30 s (alarm, displays) and 1 s (generator checks); NO VOLTAGE DATA notice after 5 s without a sample. Board: divider on A2 / AN37, HAL_SUPPLY_FITTED and SUPPLY_DIV_RATIO in hal/hal_pins.h (WIRING.md 3B)

Generator mode gen_max_pct 25 % (PC, 0..30; 0 = disabled; the AURIX ceiling is 30 %), gen_start_v 12.1 V (PC, 11.5..13), gen_idle_pct 8 % (PC, 3..15); +-2 % every 30 s, start delay 10 s, "still falling" = 0.02 V over 30 s, step down above start + 0.4 V, run 20 min, rest 1 min, SOG rise 0.5 kn within 20 s = GEAR FAULT; learned value NV slot 6 (all TO CONFIRM; the generator needs the neutral switch)
Dead reckoning x0.7 speed, limit 200 m or 10 min, then hold at 4 kn (PC: all)
TRAINING throttle 20 % (PC), 30 s spin-up
Neutral-start conditions OK 0.5 s to arm, alarm after 3 s
Watchdog 100 ms (core 0), 100 ms (CPU1), 500 ms (core 2)
Monitor heartbeat 200 ms (watched once core 0 runs; it must start within 3 s), limit margin 1 %, 2.5 s ramp
PC link timeout 3 s (PC)
Logging sync 2 s, new file 10 min / 20 MB, black box 60 s + 30 s

passages.heading: WHAT THE BOAT REMEMBERS (DATA FLASH)
passages.text: Kept after power-off, on the chip: the TRAINING result, the joystick calibration, the joystick source + button map, the last AUTO program and the boot counter (log file names). NOT kept, by design: the power limit (every power-up starts at 30 / 5 %) and the parameters changed from the Config tab.

passages.heading: WHAT THE BOAT REMEMBERS (DATA FLASH)
passages.text: * A save is written to the flash only in STANDBY (the boat not stopping): a program uploaded while driving is kept in memory and written at the next STANDBY; the screens show "NV save pending" meanwhile. The control loop never waits for the flash.

passages.heading: WHAT THE BOAT REMEMBERS (DATA FLASH)
passages.text: * Every record carries a version and a checksum. A record that is unusable (bad checksum, an older firmware format, a corrupted flash) is NOT used: the defaults take over and both screens show the notice NV DATA RESET (log event NV) - check the joystick calibration / map, the TRAINING result and the program before leaving the dock. A power loss during a write keeps the previous record. * NV FAULT (a notice, no alarm): the data flash does not work; nothing is saved any more (everything is lost at power-off), the boat drives on.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * After a power-limit drop the throttle comes down at 50 %/s (not a sudden cut), which takes up to ~1.4 s from 100 % to 30 %. * The STANDBY button works even with the stick held (the stick is then ignored until centred). The PC can't leave MANUAL at all.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * A STOP waypoint only chirps; the "ARRIVED" alarm is for the end. * The PC may acknowledge alarms in any mode (the panel button only in STANDBY). * A normally-open STANDBY button can't be pressed if its wire breaks; a normally-closed button with a line check would catch that.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * Parameters changed from the PC are lost at power-off (the joystick calibration / map, the TRAINING result and the AUTO program are kept in the data flash - chapter 15). * A new program can't be uploaded while AUTO runs.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * Joystick hand-back in a running AUTO goes to STANDBY (resume = PC + CONFIRM). * USB lever: hand-back (and HDG LOCK from MANUAL) needs the lever in the neutral zone, so the engine is at idle at the hand-back.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * USB lever: CONFIRM only needs the stick centred, not the lever. * USB joystick fault while driving: the stick that steered is gone, so the gyro holds the course while the throttle comes down at the STANDBY rate, then neutral, then steering held - same as a broken wire on the analog stick.

passages.heading: D) KNOWN LIMITATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS
passages.text: * While mapping buttons, the old map still works (TAKE takes over). * Core 2 RAM and the LMU blocks are 81-84 % full (the black box). Each new byte in the 20 Hz log record costs 1.2 KB of black box: the slot is 184 B (182 used) - a bigger record needs LOG_BB_SLOT raised and mapreport.py checked (or a shorter black box).

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.text: The details of every part are in chapter 9 ("UAV MAGAZINE - ..." sections). This chapter is the whole picture, the training and the legal note.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: WHAT IT IS
passages.text: Six small 7-inch camera drones (ArduPilot quads) stacked in the boat under a hatch, slot 1 = the top one = the next out. They are for OBSERVATION ONLY: camera, video, telemetry. No payload, no release, no other output: the gateway only sends the messages of its allow-list and registers only drones with four motors and nothing else. Every flight is ONE-WAY: a drone never lands on the boat. Charging is not part of the system.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: WHO DOES WHAT
passages.text: Copilot: registers, sends routes, prepares a launch, may fly a drone by hand from the copilot's own station at any time. Captain: approves every launch (YES / NO on screen 1), closes the hatch after a stop, may fly a drone by hand only with the boat in STANDBY (then the joystick does nothing on the boat), may take a drone over from a copilot. The boat: the ONLY thing the magazine ever asks of the boat is the hatch relay, through the normal relay table of the HELM station. The drones never touch the boat's driving, alarms or joystick.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: A LAUNCH, STEP BY STEP
passages.text: 1. Tools - UAV magazine: REGISTER the drones (read-only check). 2. Send route -> NEXT UAV (or a slot): the gateway checks altitude 10..120 m, radio range, battery with the landing reserve, no-fly zones / air geofence. 3. GPS trusted, no boat WARNING alarm, relay board OK. Any boat speed (above 5 kn: the HIGH SPEED warning - slower is safer for the take-off).

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: A LAUNCH, STEP BY STEP
passages.text: 4. PREPARE LAUNCH (copilot) -> the captain's YES on screen 1. 5. The sequence: mission upload + read-back -> hatch OPEN -> GPS -> ARM (only with the OPEN switch) -> climb -> the slot cable breaks away -> the mission starts -> the next drone after 15 s -> the hatch closes after the last.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: A LAUNCH, STEP BY STEP
passages.text: 6. Any warning stops it: no further drone, the flying ones go on, a drone still on deck is disarmed, the hatch is switched by NOTHING (the captain closes it with HATCH CLOSE). In flight: the map, the video (open = streamed, never on data saver / STARLINK), AI boxes on the video (never a speed cap), the flight logs.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: THE ONE LANDING RULE
passages.text: A drone lands ONLY at its battery minimum, where it is (over the sea the drone is lost - accepted). CAUTION 60 s and 20 s before. No GPS, no link, a warning = it HOLDS. Never RTL, never SmartRTL, never a landing on the boat.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: TRAINING
passages.text: Academy - "UAV lesson" = "UAV launch and observation": the academy's own UAV simulator inside the academy program (it uses the gateway's real launch, allow-list, route and battery rules with a simulated boat + magazine; never a gateway, a drone or a boat). Steps: register, route, STANDBY, prepare, the captain's YES, watch the launch until the hatch closes, open the video, the battery minimum. The guided tour has a chapter "The UAV magazine". Demo: START_DEMO.bat runs 6 simulated drones + the simulated hatch.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: TRAINING
passages.text: The SHORE station has the demo boat file (relay 8 = the UAV hatch): once it holds HELM in STANDBY it sends that relay table and the boat asks for the joystick CONFIRM - press CONFIRM in the ON BOARD window once; then PREPARE LAUNCH works.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: HARDWARE
passages.text: PARTS.md "UAV magazine" and WIRING.md 3H: 6 ELRS TX modules (MAVLink), 6 VRX + USB captures, powered hubs (the hub port = the slot), antennas apart, breakaway USB-C per slot, the hatch actuator on a relay board with 8 or more channels, two hatch switches read by an FT232R breakout (CTS = OPEN, DSR = CLOSED, external pull-ups). Gateway load: gateway/README.md section 26 (about +0.9 GB RAM and Quick Sync for the six video encoders).

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: THE LAW (not legal advice)
passages.text: EU Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945 apply in Greece; the authority for drones is the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority (HCAA, Greek: Αρχή Πολιτικής Αεροπορίας - ΑΠΑ; check the current name and rules before you fly). - UAS GEOGRAPHICAL ZONES (2019/947 Art. 15) and airspace: check the national drone zones and NOTAMs before every flight; near airports, heliports, military / restricted areas the flight needs the coordination / permission those zones require (air traffic services). The gateway's no-fly file is NOT the official map.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: THE LAW (not legal advice)
passages.text: - Flying beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) is the SPECIFIC category: an operational authorisation from the HCAA (SORA, or a PDRA where one fits). Take-off from a moving vessel and flights near people / vessels must be covered by that authorisation.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: THE LAW (not legal advice)
passages.text: - UAS OPERATOR REGISTRATION with the HCAA: the operator number on every drone. - DIRECT REMOTE ID broadcast (EU 2019/945, Delegated Regulation 2020/1058): a drone without a class mark needs an add-on Remote ID module, as the authorisation says. - A remote pilot with the competency the authorisation requires.

passages.chapter: UAV MAGAZINE - OVERVIEW, TRAINING AND THE LAW (step U6)
passages.heading: THE LAW (not legal advice)
passages.text: - Third-party liability INSURANCE as the authorisation and Greek law require (Regulation (EC) 785/2004 for 20 kg and more). - Radio limits: analog 5.8 GHz video 25 mW EIRP, 2.4 GHz 100 mW EIRP - they limit the range. - State / Navy operations are outside the EASA rules (Regulation 2018/1139 Art. 2(3)) and follow their own national rules. - Recordings of people: data protection (GDPR) applies. - The RESPONSIBILITY stays with the UAS operator and the remote pilot.

passages.heading: The guided tour
passages.text: This tour shows the station's two screens, the tools window, the modes, the alarms, the joystick and the panel buttons. Press Next or the right arrow to go on, Back or the left arrow to go back. The tour only explains: it never connects to a boat.

passages.heading: The rules that always win
passages.text: The STANDBY button on the boat always wins. The boat's joystick always wins over the autopilot and the PC. After every power-up the power limit is 30 percent forward and 5 percent reverse. The gear changes only at idle. Whatever changes the driving from the copilot needs the captain's ACCEPT on screen 1.

passages.heading: The driving screen
passages.text: Screen 1 shows the front camera over the whole screen with the instruments on top. The centre of the picture always stays free so you can see the sea. The captain sits here with the joystick.

passages.heading: Mode and link
passages.text: Top centre: the mode in large letters, in HDG LOCK and AUTO with the target heading. Below it the link channel, the delay, the age of the data and the power limit. If no data arrives it says NO DATA in red.

passages.heading: The MASTER lamps
passages.text: Right of the mode are the two lamps MASTER WARNING and MASTER CAUTION. They flash while an alarm is not acknowledged on this PC. Pressing a lamp silences this PC only.

passages.heading: Left mirror
passages.text: Top left: the rear left camera, like a car mirror. If the camera stops it says NO VIDEO or VIDEO FROZEN.

passages.heading: Right mirror
passages.text: Top right: the rear right camera. In MANEUVER, for the trailer and the ramp, the rear cameras are emphasised.

passages.heading: Alarms
passages.text: Under the right mirror are all alarms in one place, one per line, the most severe first. Red for a warning, amber for a caution. If they do not all fit, the last line says plus and the number of the others. An alarm you have not acknowledged flashes.

passages.heading: Notices
passages.text: Under the alarms: notices, for example that the generator is starting or that there is no voltage data. A notice never changes the mode.

passages.heading: Throttle
passages.text: Left: the throttle bar: the servo position, the power limit as a line and, if there is one, the speed cap from the navigation. The throttle goes up gently and comes down fast. In STANDBY and on every fault it goes to idle at once.

passages.heading: Speed
passages.text: Right: the speed in knots from the GPS, with its trend, and the set speed when there is one.

passages.heading: Depth
passages.text: The depth from the gateway's charts, not from a depth sounder. Without chart data the system treats the water as shallow. The charts are free data and not for navigation.

passages.heading: Waypoint
passages.text: In AUTO: the next waypoint of the route, its distance, bearing and time to go.

passages.heading: AIS traffic
passages.text: The most dangerous ship from AIS with the closest point of approach and the time to it. Careful: AIS does not show small craft, kayaks or swimmers. Always watch the camera.

passages.heading: Rate of turn
passages.text: How fast the boat is turning, in degrees per second, from the gyro.

passages.heading: G meter
passages.text: The boat's accelerations. Hard slams in the waves give the SLAMMING alarm.

passages.heading: Mini map
passages.text: A small map with the boat, the route and the AIS traffic. The big map is on screen 2.

passages.heading: Outboard angle
passages.text: The estimated angle of the outboard, starboard or port. The outboard has no angle sensor: the system estimates it from the servo's movement.

passages.heading: Off track
passages.text: In AUTO: how many metres you are right or left of the route line. In MANEUVER this place shows the gears reverse, neutral, forward: the lit one is engaged now, the framed one is what the stick asks for. In DP it shows the spot error and the thrusters.

passages.heading: Relays
passages.text: The boat's relays chosen for screen 1, for example trim. Lit means on, grey means the state is unknown. The engine relays are lamps only here.

passages.heading: Bottom bar
passages.text: Bottom: one thin bar across the whole width, in groups: language, NIGHT, fewer instruments, picture size and Aa for the text size; AR and OBSTACLES AI; LAYOUT; the recording and SAVE; on the right the battery, the generator and the mission clock. All information on the video is green; red only for an alarm.

passages.heading: SAVE
passages.text: The red SAVE button keeps the last minutes of every camera and of the log, so you can look at them later.

passages.heading: Logo
passages.text: Bottom right the logo. It never covers an instrument or an alarm.

passages.heading: Heading tape
passages.text: Above the bottom bar: the heading tape with the bow in the middle and, in HDG LOCK and AUTO, the blue mark of the target heading.

passages.heading: Language
passages.text: EL or EN: switches the screen language. Greek is the default.

passages.heading: Night
passages.text: NIGHT: dim red for the night, so you keep your night vision.

passages.heading: Declutter
passages.text: FULL, NORMAL, MINIMAL: how many instruments are shown. The mode, the speed, the throttle, the heading and the alarms are always shown.

passages.heading: Picture size
passages.text: FILL fills the screen, FIT shows the whole camera picture with black bars.

passages.heading: AR overlays
passages.text: AR: marks drawn on the video, such as the horizon, the direction of travel, the waypoint, the AIS ships and the shallow water.

passages.heading: Layout
passages.text: LAYOUT (or the key E): every instrument gets a square white frame. Drag it by the middle to move it, by the small square at the bottom right to resize it - the mirrors too. The × hides it. RESET brings back the original layout.

passages.heading: Text size
passages.text: Aa: small, normal or large text, in every window of the station. The program has only three sizes: very important, heading and information. It is kept on this computer.

passages.heading: Screen recording and keep
passages.text: SCR records both screens of this computer at a low resolution and keeps the last sixty minutes; while it records it shows ●SCR in white. It never affects driving. SAVE now keeps the screens too, like the cameras. The ●5' and ●1h buttons keep for good the last five minutes or the last hour of both screens and of the boat's four cameras at full resolution.

passages.heading: Loudhailer: TALK
passages.text: TALK: hold the button down and speak; your voice comes out of the horn on the boat, to swimmers, fishermen, divers or the coast guard. One person speaks at a time: whoever presses first. While someone else speaks the button is grey and the bar says who speaks. Next to it is the level of the boat microphone. The loudhailer never changes the driving.

passages.heading: Assistant: ASK
passages.text: ASK with the AI badge: hold the button or the F9 key and ask about the C2 by voice, such as: where do I close the hatch? Let go to ask. The assistant shows the question it heard and says the answer from the manual, the chapter first; the text is in the assistant's panel on screen 2. It is a different button from TALK, it does not listen while you hold the loudhailer, and it never sends anything to the boat.

passages.heading: OBSTACLES AI
passages.text: OBSTACLES with the AI badge: the obstacle detection by artificial intelligence, on the video. AI only warns and may slow down - it never steers.

passages.heading: Clear slowdown
passages.text: CLEAR SLOWDOWN appears only while the camera's obstacle detection holds a speed cap. Only the captain on screen 1 can clear it. The detection never steers and never raises the throttle.

passages.heading: Restore power
passages.text: RESTORE POWER appears only when slamming reduced the throttle and the sea has calmed. The boat asks first: "Calmer sea - restore power?". Only the captain's ACCEPT brings the power back, gradually. Never by itself, never from the copilot.

passages.heading: Driving from the station
passages.text: Above the screen buttons: REMOTE MANUAL, driving with the station's joystick. Only for a captain with the licence. Uncrewed boat: one press and it starts at once, only with the joystick centred and the lever at neutral. Crewed boat: someone on board presses CONFIRM on the joystick within 10 seconds. There is no release button: to stop, choose another mode, for example STANDBY, AUTO or DP.

passages.heading: MANEUVER
passages.text: MANEUVER, for the trailer, the ramp and the dock: steering and gear only, the throttle always stays at idle. The gear is on the stick: push it fully forward and hold it for a moment, about 0.3 seconds, for forward, fully back for reverse, and let it go to the centre for neutral. The throttle lever does nothing here. REMOTE MANUAL and MANEUVER switch straight to each other. The one that runs is lit.

passages.heading: YES / NO questions
passages.text: When the copilot asks for something that changes the driving, or the collision avoidance proposes a heading, a question appears in the lower part of the screen, above the bottom bar: YES on top, NO underneath. YES is already selected. The stick's trigger answers with the selection, but only once the question has been shown for half a second and only with a new press. The thumb button says NO. The stick forward or back, or the hat up or down, changes the selection. In MANEUVER the stick forward and back is the gear, so there you select with the hat. While the question is open the trigger is not sent to the boat. Without an answer in 10 seconds it is rejected.

passages.heading: The map
passages.text: Screen 2 is the map over the whole window. The boat is always in the centre, north always up, and the boat symbol turns with the heading. If you pan the map it snaps back to the boat after 10 seconds.

passages.heading: Mode bar
passages.text: Top middle, always visible: STANDBY, HDG LOCK, AUTO, REMOTE, MANEUVER, DP and MANUAL. The current mode is white with black letters. Whatever is not allowed now is grey - a click says why. A click changes the mode; the boat checks every request again. MANUAL is shown, but only the joystick on board starts it. STANDBY is the only red button.

passages.heading: BATTLE SHORT
passages.text: BATTLE SHORT - requires the commander's authorisation code.

passages.heading: Status
passages.text: Top left: the first line is the boat list with the white CONNECTED lamp. Choose a boat: the station connects, checks the boat's name by itself and takes HELM at once if it is free. Changing boats is one move. Leaving an UNCREWED boat that is moving asks once, because the boat starts its lost-link procedure. Below it the mode, the power limit, the heading, the target, the rate of turn, the gear, the throttle and the GPS. Every panel closes with a click on its title and moves when you drag the title. RESET TO DEFAULT puts them back.

passages.heading: Alarms
passages.text: Top right the alarms. This panel is always drawn, even with every other panel collapsed. The ACK ALARM button first silences this PC, then sends the acknowledge to the boat. Space or A silences this PC only.

passages.heading: HELM
passages.text: Which station holds HELM, the captain and copilot roles, take, release and swap. Only the HELM station's commands are carried out.

passages.heading: Link
passages.text: The quality of the channels 4G, RF and STARLINK, the profile CREWED or UNCREWED, the distance to the shore, the lost-link countdown and ENGINE KILLED.

passages.heading: Control
passages.text: Bottom left, above the bars: the state of the AUTO program, RETURN, the generator, DP and the captain's answers.

passages.heading: STANDBY
passages.text: The STANDBY button is in the bottom left corner and is always drawn, and on the mode bar. The copilot can always send STANDBY without ACCEPT.

passages.heading: Traffic
passages.text: Bottom right the AIS list with the collision state and the avoidance proposal.

passages.heading: Relays
passages.text: The relays of the boat file by group. Momentary ones are held down. Engine: IGNITION, START held, SHUTOFF, and RESTART.

passages.heading: Assistant: the answer
passages.text: The assistant's panel, with the AI badge, appears with the first question: the question as it was heard, the answer from the manual, how it was spoken and the whole passage with its chapter. AGAIN says it once more; IN THE MANUAL opens the manual at that place. The assistant's voice is the lowest sound: any alarm or callout cuts it at once, and while an alarm is active the answer stays text only.

passages.heading: Banners
passages.text: Top middle the banners: for example UNCREWED, shallow water ahead, collision risk, STARLINK or single-operator mode.

passages.heading: Bar 1
passages.text: Bottom, first bar: heading minus 10 and 1, the target heading, plus 1 and 10; AUTO pause, resume and skip; ROUTE, MAX SPEED and GEOFENCE open a small panel above the bar while you use them; the LINK TIME, from 3 to 60 seconds, only for the captain holding HELM (near the shore always 3); and RESTORE POWER when it is offered. The arrow on the left hides the bar, ⇅ moves it to the top or the bottom.

passages.heading: Bar 2
passages.text: Bottom, second bar: the nearest ship with its CPA, the messages, zoom, back to boat, BOAT (change boat), TRACKS and NEW TRACK, CAMERA, tools, Aa for the text size and RESET TO DEFAULT. Above the bars the note that the charts are not for navigation.

passages.heading: Camera view
passages.text: The CAMERA button shows one of the boat's cameras over the whole of screen 2, with the basic data in green. Choose FRONT or REAR on the first bar; MAP or Esc goes back to the map. The copilot gets a lighter picture, and when the link is not enough, the copilot's is cut first: the captain's video has priority. The mode bar, STANDBY and the alarms always stay.

passages.heading: Track
passages.text: The white line on the map (black on a light map) is the boat's track: every point is kept and written at once to this PC's disk, one track per boat. A click on the line shows the time and the speed at that place. NEW TRACK, after a YES or NO question, saves the track with the date, time and boat name and starts a new one. TRACKS opens the list of the saved ones: show on the map as a grey dashed line with the date, hide, remove from the map without deleting the file, GPX export and import.

passages.heading: Screen recording
passages.text: On the second bar, the recording group: SCR records both screens of this computer, the last sixty minutes. ●5' and ●1h keep for good the last five minutes or the last hour of the screens here and of the cameras on the boat. The message says what was kept, and if something was shorter than asked.

passages.heading: Loudhailer
passages.text: On the second bar, the TALK button: held down, you speak through the horn on the boat. The captain and the copilot can both speak, one at a time. The message line says who speaks. Listening, the volume and the ready messages are on the Loudhailer page of the tools.

passages.heading: Editing on the map
passages.text: Route and geofence: click adds a point, drag moves it, right click deletes it. The route is not sent until you press Send route.

passages.heading: Connection
passages.text: Connect to the boat's gateway or to the simulator, and the state of the link.

passages.heading: Control
passages.text: The commands as buttons: modes, power limit with the code and CONFIRM, alarm acknowledge.

passages.heading: Program
passages.text: The AUTO route table, up to 50 waypoints. The gateway checks shallow water and the geofence before it takes the route.

passages.heading: AIS
passages.text: Every AIS ship with its closest approach and time, details on click.

passages.heading: Plot
passages.text: A plot of the heading, the target and the steering over time.

passages.heading: Config
passages.text: The boat's parameters. They change only in STANDBY and the boat keeps its own limits.

passages.heading: Joystick
passages.text: The joystick source and button map, and the calibration. STANDBY only.

passages.heading: Cameras
passages.text: The boat's cameras and their state.

passages.heading: Remote
passages.text: The station's joystick for REMOTE MANUAL and MANEUVER: connection and check.

passages.heading: Network
passages.text: The channels 4G, RF and STARLINK with their quality and the data used.

passages.heading: System
passages.text: The state of the gateway, the logging and the boat.

passages.heading: Bench
passages.text: BENCH TEST at the dock: USB only, not moving, throttle zero and neutral, short steering pulses.

passages.heading: Engine
passages.text: IGNITION, START held for up to 5 seconds, SHUTOFF and RESTART. Only at idle and in neutral.

passages.heading: Sound
passages.text: Volume, voice and the alarm sounds. Voice: Piper, an offline AI voice, or the Windows voice of the language when one is installed; the voice samples help you choose. Warnings never go too quiet.

passages.heading: Loudhailer
passages.text: The loudhailer page. TALK with the button held down. Listen: the boat microphone plays here, with mute, volume and a white level meter; it is muted on the boat while anyone talks. Ready messages with one click, first in Greek and then in English, such as: Unmanned vessel, keep clear. The list is edited here. Sound signals: five short blasts mean danger, and one prolonged blast. The horn volume has a limit set on the gateway. On a weak link the voice drops first. Everything is recorded with the cameras. There is no VHF radio.

passages.heading: Assistant
passages.text: The page of the assistant, the talking manual: on or off on this computer, its own microphone, separate from the loudhailer, and the ask key, F9 at first; a USB foot pedal that sends the same key works the same. Below it the last question, the answer with the manual passage, how it was spoken, and the buttons AGAIN and IN THE MANUAL. It works without the internet and never records sound. If it stops it shows ASSISTANT OFF and starts again by itself; driving is never affected.

passages.heading: UAV magazine
passages.text: The UAV magazine page: six slots, slot one is the top one and goes out first. Register reads the drone through its slot's cable and checks it, read only. A drone that is not registered or fails a check is never launched, and the reason is written next to it. Observation only: no payload and no release.

passages.heading: Events
passages.text: The list of every event and the boat's answers.

passages.heading: STANDBY
passages.text: Idle, neutral, the steering holds. At power-up and after every fault. Idle and neutral first, then the steering.

passages.heading: MANUAL
passages.text: Driving with the boat's joystick. From any mode, by moving the stick or TAKE. It is left only with the stick centred.

passages.heading: HDG LOCK
passages.text: Holds the heading. Plus minus 1 and 10 degrees change it. The throttle stays on the joystick. Moving the stick sideways gives you MANUAL. Uncrewed boat: the captain holding HELM chooses it from REMOTE or MANEUVER. The throttle stays where it was and only comes down: the shore lever is a ceiling. Shallow water, the shore, a collision risk or an obstacle slow the boat, they never steer. No position or no charts, no check from the gateway, or the shore within 100 metres: it stops at idle in neutral. Outside the geofence: STANDBY. Move the shore stick sideways: you steer by hand and HDG LOCK waits. Let it go: after 2 seconds the boat returns to the old heading. Press the trigger while you steer: the heading at that moment becomes the new heading.

passages.heading: AUTO
passages.text: Follows the route. Starts with a station command and CONFIRM on the joystick within 10 seconds. The joystick interrupts it. Uncrewed boat: the captain holding HELM steers by hand with the shore stick sideways and AUTO waits; let go and after 2 seconds AUTO goes back to the route. While you steer by hand, shallow water or the shore within 100 metres, no charts or position, or no check from the gateway: it stops at idle in neutral. The shore lever is a power ceiling: it only takes power away, never adds; pull it back for less power.

passages.heading: TRAINING
passages.text: Calibration of the outboard steering. Only from STANDBY, from the station.

passages.heading: REMOTE MANUAL
passages.text: Driving with the station's joystick, up to 20 percent forward and 5 reverse. If the data is late: idle, neutral, heading hold, and STANDBY after 5 seconds.

passages.heading: BENCH TEST
passages.text: Dock test from the USB laptop. It ends by itself if the boat moves.

passages.heading: MANEUVER
passages.text: Trailer, ramp, dock: steering and gear forward, neutral, reverse. Throttle always at idle. Captain only.

passages.heading: DP
passages.text: Dynamic positioning with the small thrusters: SPOT holds the position, JOG moves a little, CRUISE and TRIP at low speed. The outboard stays at idle and in neutral.

passages.heading: MASTER WARNING
passages.text: Red lamp: something serious. A repeating tone and voice until you acknowledge it. Look at the alarm list at once.

passages.heading: MASTER CAUTION
passages.text: Amber lamp: caution. One chime and the voice once. Advisories light no lamp. Acknowledging on the station silences this PC only.
The compass is lost. In HDG LOCK and AUTO the gyro holds the heading until idle and neutral. In MANUAL alarm only.
No GPS. In AUTO it continues by dead reckoning at a lower speed.
The GPS position is not trusted, possibly spoofed or jumped. The system does not use it until it agrees again.
The dead reckoning reached its uncertainty or time limit. AUTO holds the heading slowly. Take over.
The position uncertainty is larger than the arrival radius: no arrival is declared.
AUTO reached the last waypoint.
A gear problem, for example the neutral switch does not agree. Idle and STANDBY.
The TRAINING calibration is running or needed.
The boat's joystick has a fault. The manual modes go to STANDBY, idle and neutral first.
The joystick is not centred. HDG LOCK, AUTO, REMOTE and TRAINING do not start. Let the stick centre.
The boat's joystick took control: MANUAL.
The link to the PC is lost. The power limit is lowered.
At power-up the outputs arm only with idle, neutral and the joystick centred.
The independent safety monitor tripped: idle, neutral, steering stops. It stays latched until a restart.
The control loop ran late. Report it.
The SD card does not write. Driving is not affected; the gateway keeps a copy.
The gateway PC was silent for 3 seconds. It does not change the mode.
The gateway's disk is filling up or has a problem.
The HELM station is lost. HELM goes to nobody. With a crew the mode does not change.
The link moved to another channel.
In REMOTE MANUAL the joystick data is late: idle, neutral, heading hold, STANDBY after 5 seconds. It never resumes by itself.
Hard slams in the waves. At red the throttle comes down one step. Slow down. Power never comes back by itself: when the sea calms, the boat asks the captain. Only an ACCEPT brings it back, gradually.
The AIS receiver gives no data. You see no ships on the map.
An AIS ship will pass very close. In AUTO the system slows and avoids, otherwise alarm only.
The avoidance finds no safe solution. Slow speed, same course: the driver decides.
Shallow water ahead from the charts. No chart data counts as shallow.
The camera sees an obstacle ahead. Only a slowdown in AUTO, never a turn.
The emergency stop is pressed: STANDBY and no other mode while it is pressed.
The profile changed between CREWED and UNCREWED. The power limit goes back to the start values.
Uncrewed, the link to the captain was lost for longer than the LINK TIME: STANDBY, idle and neutral. Near the shore the engine is stopped at once, at open sea after 10 seconds.
The system stopped the engine. It stays stopped until a power-up on board or a RESTART from the HELM station.
The 12 volt bank is low. It does not change the mode.
The relay board does not answer. The relay states are unknown.
A thruster is hot and rests. DP ends.
The boat is more than 15 metres off the DP spot. Too far or too long: STANDBY.
Both thrusters at maximum for 10 seconds: the wind or the current is too strong.
A servo on the CAN bus is silent or not ready: STANDBY.
A CAN bus fault: STANDBY.
Uncrewed, in HDG LOCK, the boat left the geofence: STANDBY, idle and neutral.
The station gets no data from the boat. What you see is old.

passages.heading: Stick left / right
passages.text: The stick left and right turns the outboard. From any mode, a deflection longer than 100 milliseconds gives you MANUAL.

passages.heading: Stick forward / back
passages.text: Forward and back is throttle forward and reverse. The gear changes only at idle: idle, wait, neutral, wait, new gear.

passages.heading: TAKE
passages.text: TAKE takes control at once: MANUAL, and the power limit is lowered.

passages.heading: AUTO
passages.text: With the stick centred, the joystick's AUTO button leaves MANUAL to the autopilot.

passages.heading: CONFIRM
passages.text: CONFIRM only answers a pending station request, within 10 seconds, with the stick centred. It never changes the mode by itself.

passages.heading: USB joystick and lever
passages.text: With the USB joystick the throttle lever does not return by itself. Neutral zone 45 to 55 percent. After a takeover, bring the lever to the throttle's position to pick it up.

passages.heading: STANDBY
passages.text: The STANDBY button on the boat always wins, in every mode. No PC can override it. In STANDBY it acknowledges the alarms.

passages.heading: HDG LOCK
passages.text: Locks the current heading. Only with the stick centred, otherwise it refuses with a chirp.

passages.heading: Minus 1
passages.text: One degree to port on the target heading.

passages.heading: Plus 1
passages.text: One degree to starboard on the target heading.

passages.heading: Minus 10
passages.text: Ten degrees to port on the target heading.

passages.heading: Plus 10
passages.text: Ten degrees to starboard on the target heading. Uncrewed, the panel course buttons are ignored.

passages.heading: Emergency stop
passages.text: The red emergency stop: STANDBY, and no other mode while it is pressed. After the tour, go on with the simulator lessons.

passages.heading: Registering a UAV
passages.text: On the UAV magazine page, the REGISTER button of each slot reads the drone through the slot cable and checks its settings without changing anything. A failure means that drone is not launched.

passages.heading: Observation only
passages.text: The boat's drones are observation cameras only. The gateway sends only the messages of an allow list and accepts only drones with four motors and no other output.

passages.heading: UAV route and the map
passages.text: Sending a route asks where to: the boat, the next UAV, a UAV in the magazine or a flying one. The gateway checks altitude, radio range, battery with the landing reserve and no-fly zones. Every UAV is on the map with its picture, its track and altitude, battery, link.

passages.heading: Preparing a launch
passages.text: The copilot presses PREPARE LAUNCH and the captain answers YES or NO on screen 1. A launch is allowed at any speed; above five knots the station warns of high speed. The drones go out one by one, from the top slot.

passages.heading: STOP and the hatch
passages.text: STOP ends the sequence: no further drone, the flying ones go on. ARM happens only with the hatch OPEN switch. After a stop the hatch stays as it is, and only the captain closes it with HATCH CLOSE.

passages.heading: UAV video and AI
passages.text: A click on a drone opens its video over the whole of screen 2. The station gets the video only while it is open, and never on the data saver. The AI obstacle detection only shows boxes on the drone video and never slows the boat.

passages.heading: The only landing
passages.text: A drone lands only at its battery minimum, where it is. A notice sixty and twenty seconds before. Without GPS or without a link it just holds. Never a return, never a landing on the boat.

passages.heading: Flying a UAV with the joystick
passages.text: The FLY UAV button gives the joystick to the drone, with the JOYSTICK to UAV banner on both screens and the drone's green HUD on screen 1. The captain flies only with the boat in STANDBY. RETURN TO BOAT gives the joystick back and the drone holds.

passages.heading: Flight logs
passages.text: Every flight is written to its own file. FLIGHT LOGS lists them and the export is CSV or GPX.

passages.heading: The law
passages.text: Flight beyond visual line of sight is in the specific category: an authorisation from the civil aviation authority, a registered operator, a competent remote pilot, direct remote ID, the UAS geographical zones and insurance. The responsibility is the operator's and the remote pilot's.
